sentences.zh: 文昌帝君祭纛祀砲京師群祀附五祀八蜡直省祭厲

translations.literal: Lord Wenchang; sacrifice to the battle standard; cannon sacrifice; collective sacrifices in the capital; appended: the Five Sacrifices and the Eight La; provincial sacrifices to wandering spirits
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wenchang; sacrifice to the battle standard; cannon sacrifice; collective sacrifices in the capital; appended: the Five Sacrifices and the Eight La; provincial sacrifices to wandering spirits

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王廟順治初，建都城西阜成門內，南鄉，正中景德崇聖殿，九楹，東西二廡各七楹，燎爐各一。

translations.literal: Temple of Emperors of Successive Dynasties: In the early Shunzhi reign, it was built inside Fucheng Gate on the west side of the capital, facing south. At the center was the Jingde Chongsheng Hall, of nine bays; the east and west covered corridors each had seven bays, with one offering furnace apiece.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi period a Temple of Emperors of Successive Dynasties was erected inside Fucheng Gate on the west side of the capital, facing south. Its main hall, the Jingde Chongsheng Hall, had nine bays; flanking covered corridors on the east and west each had seven bays, with one offering furnace on each side.

sentences.zh: 後為祭器庫，前景德門。

translations.literal: Behind it was a repository for ritual vessels, and in front stood the Jingde Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Behind stood a storehouse for ritual vessels, and in front the Jingde Gate.

sentences.zh: 門外神庫、神廚、宰牲亭、井亭、鐘樓、齋所咸備。

translations.literal: Outside the gate were fully provided a spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, slaughter pavilion, well pavilion, bell tower, and fasting lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate were a full complement of ancillary buildings: spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, slaughter pavilion, well pavilion, bell tower, and fasting lodge.

sentences.zh: 初，明祀歷代帝王，元世祖入廟，遼、金諸帝不與焉。

translations.literal: Initially, under the Ming, when successive emperors were worshipped, Kublai Khan was admitted to the temple, while the emperors of Liao and Jin were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, worship in the temple had included Kublai Khan but excluded the rulers of Liao and Jin.

sentences.zh: 至是用禮臣言，以遼、金分統宋時天下，其太祖應廟祀。

translations.literal: At this time, following the advice of the Board of Rites, because Liao and Jin had each ruled the realm during the Song period, their founding ancestors were deemed fit for temple worship.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the recommendation of the Board of Rites, the founding ancestors of Liao and Jin were admitted, on the ground that each dynasty had held sway over the realm during Song times.

sentences.zh: 元啟疆宇，功始太祖，禮合追崇。

translations.literal: The Yuan had opened their territory, and the achievement began with their founding ancestor; ritual propriety called for posthumous elevation.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan had opened new territory, and their achievement began with the founding ancestor; by ritual propriety he deserved posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 從祀諸臣，若遼耶律赫嚕，金尼瑪哈、斡里雅布，元穆呼哩、巴延，明徐達、劉基併入之。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers worshipped with them included, from Liao, Yelü Helu; from Jin, Nimaha and Waliyabu; from Yuan, Muhuli and Bayan; and from Ming, Xu Da and Liu Ji—all were admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Among the attendant ministers newly admitted were Yelü Helu of Liao; Nimaha and Waliyabu of Jin; Muhuli and Bayan of the Yuan; and Xu Da and Liu Ji of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 屆日，大臣一人祭正殿，殿祀伏羲，神農，黃帝，少昊，顓頊，帝嚳，唐堯，虞舜，夏禹，商湯，周武王，漢高祖、光武，唐太宗，宋、遼、金太祖、世宗，元太祖、世祖，明太祖，凡廿一帝，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, one senior minister sacrificed in the main hall. The hall enshrined Fuxi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diku, Tang Yao, Yu Shun, Yu of Xia, Tang of Shang, King Wu of Zhou, Han Gaozu and Guangwu, Tang Taizong, the founding ancestors and Shizong of Song, Liao, and Jin, the founding ancestors and Shizu of Yuan, and Ming Taizu—in all twenty-one emperors, sacrificed to with the tai lao offering.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day a senior minister sacrificed in the main hall to twenty-one sovereigns: Fuxi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diku, Tang Yao, Yu Shun, Yu of Xia, Tang of Shang, King Wu of Zhou, Han Gaozu and Guangwu, Tang Taizong, the founding ancestors and Shizong of Song, Liao, and Jin, the Yuan founders and Shizu, and Ming Taizu—with the grand tai lao offering.

sentences.zh: 分獻官四人祭兩廡，廡祀風后、力牧、皋陶、夔、龍、伯益、伯夷、伊尹、傅說、周公旦、召公奭、太公望、召虎、方叔、張良、蕭何、曹參、陳平、周勃、鄧禹、馮異、諸葛亮、房玄齡、杜如晦、李靖、郭子儀、李晟、張巡、許遠、耶律赫嚕、曹彬、潘美、張浚、韓世忠、岳飛、尼瑪哈、斡里雅布、穆呼哩、巴延、徐達、劉基，凡功臣四十一，祀以少牢。

translations.literal: Four distributing officers sacrificed in the two side halls, which enshrined Fenghou, Limu, Gao Yao, Kui, Long, Bo Yi, Boyi, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, Duke of Zhou Dan, Duke of Shao Shi, Taigong Wang, Zhaohu, Fangshu, Zhang Liang, Xiao He, Cao Shen, Chen Ping, Zhou Bo, Deng Yu, Feng Yi, Zhuge Liang, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Li Jing, Guo Ziyi, Li Sheng, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Yelü Helu, Cao Bin, Pan Mei, Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, Yue Fei, Nimaha, Waliyabu, Muhuli, Bayan, Xu Da, and Liu Ji—in all forty-one meritorious ministers, sacrificed to with the xiao lao offering.
translations.idiomatic: Four distributing officers sacrificed in the east and west side halls to forty-one meritorious ministers, from Fenghou and Limu through Bo Yi, Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Taigong Wang, Zhang Liang, Zhuge Liang, Fang Xuanling, Guo Ziyi, Yue Fei, and down to Xu Da and Liu Ji—with the lesser xiao lao offering.

sentences.zh: 十四年，聖祖躬祭，屆時致齋畢，翼日昧爽，駕出西華門，至廟降，入幄次盥訖，入直殿就位上香。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Sacred Ancestor personally performed the sacrifice. When the appointed day arrived and the fasting observance was complete, at dawn on the following day the imperial carriage issued from Xihua Gate, proceeded to the temple and alighted, entered the curtained enclosure to perform ablutions, then entered the main hall, took his place, and offered incense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Kangxi performed the sacrifice in person. After completing the fast, at dawn the next day he left by Xihua Gate, entered the temple, washed in the curtained enclosure, and took his place in the main hall to offer incense.

sentences.zh: 三皇位前，二跪六拜，奠帛、爵，讀祝，俱初獻時行。

translations.literal: Before the tablets of the three earliest sovereigns he performed two kneelings and six prostrations, presented silk and libation cups, and read the prayer—all at the time of the initial offering.
translations.idiomatic: Before the tablets of the three earliest sovereigns he knelt twice and bowed six times, presented silk and libation cups, and read the prayer, all during the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 凡三獻，分獻官祀兩廡如儀。

translations.literal: There were three offerings in all; distributing officers sacrificed in the two side halls according to the prescribed rite.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings were made in all, while distributing officers sacrificed in the side halls according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 遣官則衣朝服。

translations.literal: When an envoy was dispatched, he wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was performed by a dispatched official, he wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 王、公承祭，入景德左門，升左階，位階上，餘入右門，位階下，俱三跪九拜，不飲酒、受胙，不陪祀。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes who undertook the sacrifice entered the left Jingde Gate, ascended the left steps, and took their places on the upper steps; the rest entered the right gate and took their places on the lower steps. All performed three kneelings and nine prostrations, but did not drink wine, receive sacrificial meat, or attend as accompanying sacrificers.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes conducting the sacrifice entered by the left Jingde Gate, mounted the left steps, and stood on the upper landing; others entered by the right gate and stood below. All performed three kneelings and nine prostrations but neither drank the ritual wine nor received sacrificial meat, and did not attend as accompanying sacrificers.

sentences.zh: 十七年，禮臣議言廟祀帝王，止及開創，應增守成令辟，並罷宋臣潘美、張浚祀，從之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Board of Rites proposed that temple worship of emperors had hitherto extended only to founders, and that accomplished rulers who had preserved the dynasty should be added, while the worship of the Song ministers Pan Mei and Zhang Jun should be discontinued. The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Board of Rites argued that the temple had honored only founding rulers and should also include accomplished sovereigns who had preserved their dynasties, while the Song ministers Pan Mei and Zhang Jun should be removed from worship. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是增祀商中宗、高宗，周成王、康王，漢文帝，宋仁宗，明孝宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon were added to worship Zhongzong and Gaozong of Shang; Cheng and Kang of Zhou; Wendi of Han; Renzong of Song; and Xiaozong of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The court accordingly added Zhongzong and Gaozong of Shang, Cheng and Kang of Zhou, Emperor Wen of Han, Emperor Renzong of Song, and the Ming Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 而遼、金、元太祖皆罷祀。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the founding ancestors of Liao, Jin, and Yuan were all removed from worship.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the founding ancestors of Liao, Jin, and Yuan were all removed from the temple.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嗣服，以開創功復之。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor succeeded to the throne, he restored them on account of their founding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangxi came to the throne, he restored them in recognition of their founding achievements.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，諭：「帝王崇祀，代止一二君，或廟饗其臣子而不及其君父，是偏也。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, an edict stated: "In the exalted worship of emperors, each dynasty has been limited to one or two rulers, or the temple has honored their ministers and sons without honoring their sovereign fathers—this is partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixty-first year Kangxi decreed: "In honoring emperors in the temple, each dynasty has been limited to one or two rulers, or ministers and sons have been worshipped while their sovereign fathers were not—this is partial.

sentences.zh: 凡為天下主，除亡國暨無道被弒，悉當廟祀。

translations.literal: All who have been lords of the realm, except those of fallen states and the lawless who were assassinated, should receive temple worship.
translations.idiomatic: Every ruler of the realm, except those of fallen states and the wicked who were murdered, deserves a place in the temple.

sentences.zh: 有明國事，壞自萬曆、泰昌、天啟三朝，神宗、光宗、憙宗不應崇祀，咎不在愍帝也。」

translations.literal: In the case of the Ming state, ruin began in the three reigns of Wanli, Taichang, and Tianqi; Shenzong, Guangzong, and Xizong should not be exalted in worship—the blame does not lie with the Chongzhen Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: As for the Ming, the state declined under Wanli, Taichang, and Tianqi; Shenzong, Guangzong, and Xizong should not be honored in the temple—the fault does not lie with the Chongzhen Emperor."

sentences.zh: 於是廷臣議正殿增祀夏啟、仲康、少康、杼、槐、芒、泄、不降、扃、廑、孔甲、皋、發，商太甲、沃丁、太庚、小甲、雍己、太戊、仲丁、外壬、河亶甲、祖乙、祖辛、沃甲、祖丁、南庚、陽甲、盤庚、小辛、小乙、武丁、祖庚、祖甲、廩辛、庚丁、太丁、帝乙，周成王、康王、昭王、穆王、共王、懿王、孝王、夷王、宣王、平王、桓王、庄王、僖王、惠王、襄王、頃王、匡王、定王、簡王、靈王、景王、悼王、敬王、元王、貞定王、考王、威烈王、安王、烈王、顯王、慎靚王，漢惠帝、文帝、景帝、武帝、昭帝、宣帝、元帝、成帝、哀帝、明帝、章帝、和帝、殤帝、安帝、順帝、沖帝、桓帝、靈帝、昭烈帝，唐高祖、高宗、睿宗、玄宗、肅宗、代宗、德宗、順宗、穆宗、文宗、武宗、宣宗、懿宗、僖宗，遼太宗、景宗、聖宗、興宗、道宗，宋太宗、真宗、仁宗、英宗、神宗、哲宗、高宗、孝宗、光宗、寧宗、理宗、度宗、端宗，金太宗、章宗、宣宗，元太宗、定宗、憲宗、成宗、武宗、仁宗、泰定帝、文宗、寧宗，明成祖、仁宗、宣宗、英宗、景帝、憲宗、孝宗、武宗、世宗、穆宗、愍帝，凡百四十三位。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court ministers deliberated on adding to the main hall the worship of Qi, Zhongkang, Shaokang, Zhu, Huai, Mang, Xie, Bujiang, Jiong, Jian, Kong Jia, Gao, and Fa of Xia; Tai Jia, Wo Ding, Tai Geng, Xiao Jia, Yong Ji, Tai Wu, Zhong Ding, Wai Ren, He Dan Jia, Zu Yi, Zu Xin, Wo Jia, Zu Ding, Nan Geng, Yang Jia, Pan Geng, Xiao Xin, Xiao Yi, Wu Ding, Zu Geng, Zu Jia, Lin Xin, Geng Ding, Tai Ding, and Di Yi of Shang; Cheng, Kang, Zhao, Mu, Gong, Yi, Xiao, Yi, Xuan, Ping, Huan, Zhuang, Xi, Hui, Xiang, Qing, Kuang, Ding, Jian, Ling, Jing, Dao, Jing, Yuan, Zhending, Kao, Weilie, An, Lie, Xian, and Shen Jing of Zhou; Huidi, Wendi, Jingdi, Wudi, Zhaodi, Xuandi, Yuandi, Chengdi, Aidi, Mingdi, Zhangdi, Hedi, Shangdi, Andi, Shundi, Chongdi, Huandi, Lingdi, and Zhaolie of Han; Gaozu, Gaozong, Ruizong, Xuanzong, Suzong, Daizong, Dezong, Shunzong, Muzong, Wenzong, Wuzong, Xuanzong, Yizong, and Xizong of Tang; Taizong, Jingzong, Shengzong, Xingzong, and Daozong of Liao; Taizong, Zhenzong, Renzong, Yingzong, Shenzong, Zhezong, Gaozong, Xiaozong, Guangzong, Ningzong, Lizong, Duzong, and Duanzong of Song; Taizong, Zhangzong, and Xuanzong of Jin; Taizong, Dingzong, Xianzong, Chengzong, Wuzong, Renzong, the Taiding Emperor, Wenzong, and Ningzong of Yuan; Chengzu, Renzong, Xuanzong, Yingzong, the Jing Emperor, Xianzong, Xiaozong, Wuzong, Shizong, Muzong, and the Min Emperor of Ming—in all one hundred forty-three persons.
translations.idiomatic: The court then proposed adding to the main hall one hundred forty-three sovereigns: thirteen Xia rulers from Qi through Fa; twenty-eight Shang rulers from Tai Jia through Di Yi; thirty-five Zhou rulers from Cheng through Shen Jing; nineteen Han emperors from Huidi through Zhaolie; fourteen Tang emperors from Gaozu through Xizong; five Liao emperors; thirteen Song emperors; three Jin emperors; nine Yuan emperors; and eleven Ming emperors from Chengzu through the Min Emperor.

sentences.zh: 其從祀功臣，增黃帝臣倉頡，商仲虺，周畢公高、呂侯、仲山甫、尹吉甫，漢劉章、魏相、丙吉、耿弇、馬援、趙雲，唐狄仁傑、宋璟、姚崇、李泌、陸贄、裴度，宋呂蒙正、李沆、寇準、王曾、范仲淹、富弼、韓琦、文彥博、司馬光、李綱、趙鼎、文天祥，金呼嚕，元博果密、托克托，明常遇春、李文忠、楊士奇、楊榮、于謙、李賢、劉大夏，凡四十人。

translations.literal: Among the attendant meritorious ministers, there were added Cangjie, minister of the Yellow Emperor; Zhong Hui of Shang; the Duke of Bi Gao, Marquis of Lü, Zhong Shanfu, and Yin Jifu of Zhou; Liu Zhang, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Geng Yan, Ma Yuan, and Zhao Yun of Han; Di Renjie, Song Jing, Yao Chong, Li Mi, Lu Zhi, and Pei Du of Tang; Lü Mengzheng, Li Hang, Kou Zhun, Wang Zeng, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, Han Qi, Wen Yanbo, Sima Guang, Li Gang, Zhao Ding, and Wen Tianxiang of Song; Hulu of Jin; Boguomi and Tokto of Yuan; and Chang Yuchun, Li Wenzhong, Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Yu Qian, Li Xian, and Liu Daxia of Ming—in all forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Forty meritorious ministers were also added to the side halls: Cangjie of the Yellow Emperor's court; Zhong Hui of Shang; the Duke of Bi, the Marquis of Lü, Zhong Shanfu, and Yin Jifu of Zhou; Liu Zhang, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Geng Yan, Ma Yuan, and Zhao Yun of Han; Di Renjie, Song Jing, Yao Chong, Li Mi, Lu Zhi, and Pei Du of Tang; Lü Mengzheng, Li Hang, Kou Zhun, Wang Zeng, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, Han Qi, Wen Yanbo, Sima Guang, Li Gang, Zhao Ding, and Wen Tianxiang of Song; Hulu of Jin; Boguomi and Tokto of Yuan; and Chang Yuchun, Li Wenzhong, Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Yu Qian, Li Xian, and Liu Daxia of Ming.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世宗御極，依議行，增置神主，為文鑱之石。

translations.literal: That year, when Shizong ascended the throne, the proposal was carried out: spirit tablets were added, and stone steles were carved with inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Yongzheng came to the throne, the court implemented the proposal, adding spirit tablets and carving their inscriptions on stone.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，諡明建文帝曰恭閔惠皇帝，廟祀之，位次太祖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, the Jianwen Emperor of the Ming was posthumously titled Emperor Gongminhui and admitted to temple worship, his place ranking next to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's first year the Ming Jianwen Emperor received the posthumous title Emperor Gongminhui and was admitted to the temple, ranking next to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 復定帝王廟鹿脯、鹿醢，增鹿一，兩廡易醓醢，增豕一。

translations.literal: The offerings of venison and minced venison for the Temple of Emperors were re-fixed: one deer was added; in the two side halls pickled meat was replaced with minced meat, and one pig was added.
translations.idiomatic: The temple's offerings were adjusted: an additional deer for venison and minced venison in the main hall, and in the side halls pickled meat was replaced with minced meat with an additional pig.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以唐、虞五臣唯契未祀，乃建殿成湯廟後，有司致饗，如孔廟崇聖祠制。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because among the five ministers of Tang and Yu only Qi had not yet been worshipped, a hall was built behind the temple of Cheng Tang, where the responsible officials performed offerings, following the model of the Chongsheng Shrine in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, since Qi alone among the five ministers of the Tang and Yu era had not been worshipped, a hall was built behind Cheng Tang's shrine where officials made offerings, following the Chongsheng Shrine model in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 初，帝王廟正殿用青綠琉璃瓦，至十八年重修，改覆黃瓦。

translations.literal: Initially the main hall of the Temple of Emperors used green glazed tiles; when it was rebuilt in the eighteenth year, yellow tiles were used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the main hall had green glazed tiles; when it was rebuilt in the eighteenth year, it was roofed in yellow tiles instead.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，諭廷臣：「曩時皇祖敕議增祀，聖訓至公，而陳議者未能曲體，乃列遼、金二朝，而遺東西晉、元魏、前後五代。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, the emperor instructed the court: "When my imperial grandfather formerly ordered deliberation on adding to worship, his sacred instruction was utterly fair, yet those who submitted proposals failed to embody it fully: they listed the two dynasties of Liao and Jin while omitting Eastern and Western Jin, Northern Wei, and the Five Dynasties before and after.
translations.idiomatic: In his forty-ninth year Qianlong told the court: "When my grandfather ordered deliberation on expanding the temple, his instruction was perfectly fair, yet the proposals did not fully carry it out: they included Liao and Jin but left out Eastern and Western Jin, Northern Wei, and the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 謂南北朝偏安，則遼、金亦未奄有中夏。

translations.literal: If one says the Northern and Southern Dynasties held only partial sway, then Liao and Jin likewise did not fully possess the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: If the Northern and Southern Dynasties are dismissed as merely holding partial sway, then Liao and Jin did not fully rule the Central Realm either.

sentences.zh: 即兩晉諸代，因篡而斥，不知三國正統，本在昭烈。

translations.literal: As for the several reigns of the Two Jin, they were rejected because of usurpation, without recognizing that the legitimate succession of the Three Kingdoms lay originally with Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Two Jin, they were excluded for usurpation, yet the legitimate line of the Three Kingdoms lay with Liu Bei, the Zhaolie Emperor.

sentences.zh: 至司馬氏以還，南朝神器數易，宋武帝手移晉祚，篡奪無所逃罪，其他祖宗得國不正，子孫但能守成，即為中主。

translations.literal: From the time of the Sima clan onward, the imperial regalia of the Southern Dynasties changed hands many times; Emperor Wu of Song personally transferred the Jin mandate, and usurpation admits no escape from guilt—yet for other ancestors who gained the realm improperly, if their descendants could merely preserve what they received, they count as moderate rulers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Sima clan onward the southern throne changed hands repeatedly; Emperor Wu of Song seized the Jin mandate by force, a crime that cannot be denied—yet other founders who gained power improperly may still have descendants who preserved the realm, and such rulers deserve recognition as moderate sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 且蜀漢至初唐不乏賢君，安可闕略！

translations.literal: Moreover, from Shu-Han down to early Tang there was no lack of worthy rulers—how can they be omitted!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from Shu-Han through early Tang there were many worthy rulers—how can they be left out!

sentences.zh: 洎硃溫以下，或起寇竊，或為叛臣，五十餘年，國統不絕如線。

translations.literal: From Zhu Wen onward, some rose through banditry and theft, others were rebel ministers; for more than fifty years the dynastic succession hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhu Wen onward some founders were bandits and others rebel ministers; for more than fifty years the imperial line hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 周世宗藉餘業，擴疆宇，卓然可稱，而斥擯弗列，此數百年間，祀典闃如，又豈千秋公論？

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Zhou built on inherited achievement and expanded the realm—eminently praiseworthy—yet he was rejected and not listed; for these several centuries the sacrificial canon has been silent—can this accord with the judgment of the ages?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou built on what he inherited and expanded the realm—clearly worthy of honor—yet he was excluded; for centuries the sacrificial canon has been empty of them—is that the judgment history will accept?

sentences.zh: 他若元魏雄據河北，太武、道武，胥勤治理，並宜表章。

translations.literal: Others, such as Northern Wei, which held Hebei in strength—Taizu Daowu and Shizu Taiwu all labored diligently in governance—and should likewise be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei, which dominated Hebei—both Daowu and Taiwu governed diligently—should also be honored.

sentences.zh: 昔楊維楨著正統辨，謂正統在宋不在遼、金、元，其說甚當。

translations.literal: Formerly Yang Weizhen wrote the Discourse on Legitimate Succession, holding that legitimacy lay with Song and not with Liao, Jin, or Yuan—his argument is very apt.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhen once argued in his Discourse on Legitimate Succession that legitimacy belonged to Song, not to Liao, Jin, or Yuan—and he was right.

sentences.zh: 今通禮祀遼、金，黜兩晉諸代，使後世疑本朝區分南北，非禮意也。

translations.literal: Now the comprehensive rites worship Liao and Jin while demoting the several reigns of the Two Jin, leading posterity to suspect that our dynasty distinguishes north from south—this is not the intent of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To worship Liao and Jin in the comprehensive rites while excluding the Two Jin would make posterity suspect our dynasty of favoring north over south—which is not what ritual intends.

sentences.zh: 明神、憙二宗，法紀墜失，愍帝嗣統，事無可為，雖國覆身殉，未可以荒淫例。

translations.literal: The Ming Shenzong and Xizong let law and discipline fall away; the Min Emperor inherited the succession when nothing more could be done—though the state perished and he died for it, he cannot be classed with the dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Shenzong and Xizong let law and discipline collapse; the Chongzhen Emperor inherited a hopeless situation—though the state fell and he died with it, he cannot be lumped with the dissolute.

sentences.zh: 皇祖徹神、憙，祀愍帝，具見大公。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather removed Shenzong and Xizong and worshipped the Min Emperor—fully displaying great impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi removed Shenzong and Xizong and worshipped the Chongzhen Emperor—a mark of true impartiality.

sentences.zh: 乃議者因復推祀桓、靈，亦思漢之所由亡乎？

translations.literal: Yet the deliberators now propose again to worship Huan and Ling—have they considered by what means Han perished?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deliberators now propose restoring Huan and Ling—have they considered how Han fell?

sentences.zh: 其再詳議。」

translations.literal: Let them deliberate again in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Let them deliberate again in detail."

sentences.zh: 尋議增祀兩晉、元魏、前後五代各帝王，並以唐憲宗平亂，金哀宗殉國，亦宜列祀。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter it was proposed to add worship of the emperors of the Two Jin, Northern Wei, and the Five Dynasties before and after, and because Tang Xianzong quelled rebellion and Jin Aizong died for the state, they too should be listed for worship.
translations.idiomatic: The court then proposed adding the emperors of the Two Jin, Northern Wei, and the Five Dynasties, and because Tang Xianzong quelled rebellion and Jin Aizong died for his state, they too should be admitted.

sentences.zh: 允行。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，以散宜生配饗，位次畢公高。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, San Yisheng was added to the attendant sacrifice, ranking after the Duke of Bi Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi's fourth year San Yisheng was added to the attendant sacrifice, ranking after the Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 高允配饗，位次趙雲。

translations.literal: Gao Yun was added to the attendant sacrifice, ranking after Zhao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun was added to the attendant sacrifice, ranking after Zhao Yun.

sentences.zh: 陵寢之祭，太宗征明，至燕京，即遣貝勒阿巴泰等赴金太祖、世宗陵致祭。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at imperial tombs: When Taizong campaigned against the Ming and reached Yanjing, he immediately dispatched the beile Abatai and others to offer sacrifice at the tombs of the Jin founding ancestor and Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at imperial tombs: When Hong Taiji campaigned against the Ming and reached Yanjing, he sent the beile Abatai and others to sacrifice at the tombs of the Jin founders.

sentences.zh: 順治建元，禮葬明崇禎帝、後，復詔明十二陵絜禋祀，禁樵牧，給地畝，置司香官及陵戶。

translations.literal: When Shunzhi established his reign title, the Chongzhen Emperor and empress of the Ming were buried with full rites; an edict also ordered pure sacrificial worship at the twelve Ming tombs, forbade cutting wood and grazing, allotted land by the mu, and established incense officers and tomb households.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Shunzhi reign the Chongzhen Emperor and his empress were buried with full honors; an edict also ordered proper seasonal sacrifice at the twelve Ming tombs, forbade woodcutting and grazing, allotted land, and appointed incense officers and tomb households.

sentences.zh: 歲時祭品，戶部設之。

translations.literal: Seasonal offerings were supplied by the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue supplied the seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 明年，定春、秋仲日致祭，遣官行。

translations.literal: The following year, it was fixed that sacrifice should be performed on the mid-days of spring and autumn, carried out by dispatched officials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court fixed sacrifice on the mid-days of spring and autumn, performed by dispatched officials.

sentences.zh: 六年，定明陵仍設太監，並置房山、金陵陵戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, it was fixed that eunuch superintendents should remain at the Ming tombs, and tomb households were established at Fangshan and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year eunuch superintendents were retained at the Ming tombs, and tomb households were established at Fangshan and Jinling.

sentences.zh: 八年，定帝王陵寢祀典，淮寧伏羲，滑縣顓頊、帝嚳，內黃商中宗，西華商高宗，孟津漢光武，鄭周世宗，鞏宋太祖、太宗、真宗、仁宗，趙城女媧，榮河商湯，曲阜少昊，東平唐堯，中都軒轅，咸陽周文、武、成、康，涇陽漢高祖、唐宣宗，咸寧漢文帝，長安宣帝，富平後魏孝文帝，三原唐高祖，醴泉太宗，蒲城憲宗，酃神農，寧遠虞舜，會稽夏禹，江寧明太祖，廣寧遼太祖，房山金太祖、世宗，宛平元太祖、世祖，昌平明宣宗、孝宗、世宗，各就地饗殿行之，或因陵寢築壇，惟元陵望祭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the sacrificial canon for imperial tombs was fixed: Fuxi at Huaining; Zhuanxu and Diku at Huaxian; Zhongzong of Shang at Neihuang; Gaozong of Shang at Xihua; Guangwu of Han at Mengjin; Shizong of Zhou at Zheng; Taizu, Taizong, Zhenzong, and Renzong of Song at Gong; Nüwa at Zhaocheng; Tang of Shang at Ronghe; Shaohao at Qufu; Yao at Dongping; Xuanyuan at Zhongdu; Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang of Zhou at Xianyang; Gaozu of Han and Xuanzong of Tang at Jingyang; Wendi of Han at Xianning; Xuandi of Han at Chang'an; Xiaowendi of Later Wei at Fuping; Gaozu of Tang at Sanyuan; Taizong of Tang at Liquan; Xianzong of Tang at Pucheng; Shennong at Ling; Shun at Ningyuan; Yu of Xia at Kuaiji; Taizu of Ming at Jiangning; Taizu of Liao at Guangning; Taizu and Shizong of Jin at Fangshan; Taizu and Shizu of Yuan at Wanping; Xuanzong, Xiaozong, and Shizong of Ming at Changping—at each site the rite was performed in a local offering hall, or an altar was built at the tomb, except for the Yuan tombs, which received distant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the court fixed tomb sacrifices at sites across the realm—from Fuxi at Huaining and the Song founders at Gong to Yu at Kuaiji and the Ming founders at Jiangning and Changping—each performed in a local offering hall or at an altar by the tomb; only the Yuan tombs received distant sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 十六年，幸畿輔，親酹崇禎帝陵，諡曰庄烈愍皇帝。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, while touring the capital region, he personally poured libation at the tomb of the Chongzhen Emperor and granted the posthumous title Emperor Zhuangliemin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, touring the capital region, he personally poured libation at the Chongzhen Emperor's tomb and granted the posthumous title Emperor Zhuangliemin.

sentences.zh: 凡巡幸所蒞，皆祭陵、廟，有大慶典，祭告亦如之。

translations.literal: Wherever imperial tours arrived, tombs and temples were sacrificed to; on great celebrations, sacrificial announcements were made likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the emperor traveled he sacrificed at tombs and temples; on great celebrations he made sacrificial announcements as well.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十一年，滇亂平，遣官致祭，頒冊文、香、帛，給黃傘一，御仗、龍纛各二，凡成武功，皆祭如典。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kangxi, when the Yunnan rebellion was pacified, officials were dispatched to offer sacrifice; patent texts, incense, and silk were issued, one yellow parasol was granted, and two imperial staffs and dragon banners apiece—whenever military achievement was completed, sacrifice followed the canon.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's twenty-first year, after the Yunnan rebellion was pacified, officials were sent to sacrifice with patent texts, incense, and silk, a yellow parasol, and imperial staffs and dragon banners—whenever military success was achieved, sacrifice followed ritual.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，南巡，道江寧，詣明太祖陵，拜奠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on a southern tour, passing through Jiangning, he proceeded to the tomb of Ming Taizu and bowed in offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, on a southern tour through Jiangning, he visited the tomb of Ming Taizu and bowed in offering.

sentences.zh: 諭有司巡察，守陵人防護。

translations.literal: He instructed the responsible officials to inspect and the tomb guardians to protect the site.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to inspect the site and tomb guardians to protect it.

sentences.zh: 越五年，巡會稽，祭禹陵，祝文書御名，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: Five years later, touring Kuaiji, he sacrificed at the tomb of Yu; the prayer text bore the imperial name, and he performed the rite of three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, touring Kuaiji, he sacrificed at Yu's tomb; the prayer bore the imperial name, and he performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 蹕江寧，祭明太祖陵，如祀禹儀。

translations.literal: Halting at Jiangning, he sacrificed at the tomb of Ming Taizu with the same rite used for Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning he sacrificed at Ming Taizu's tomb with the same rite used for Yu.

sentences.zh: 凡時巡祭帝王陵寢，儀同祭廟，率二跪六拜，茲蓋殊典雲。

translations.literal: Whenever touring sacrifices were made at imperial tombs, the rite was the same as temple sacrifice, generally two kneelings and six prostrations—this was a special canon.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, sacrifice at emperors' tombs followed temple ritual, generally two kneelings and six prostrations—a special practice.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，復南巡，見明太祖陵圮剝，詔依周封杞、宋例，授明裔一官，俾世守弗替。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, on another southern tour, seeing the tomb of Ming Taizu ruined and weathered, he decreed that following the Zhou precedent of enfeoffing Qi and Song, one office should be granted to a Ming descendant to guard the tomb in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, on another southern tour, seeing Ming Taizu's tomb in ruins, he decreed that following the Zhou precedent of enfeoffing Qi and Song, a Ming descendant should receive an office to guard the tomb in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，西巡，遣祭女媧氏陵，幸陝，遣祭所經諸陵，惟祀周文、武祝文書御名，尊聖也。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, on a western tour, he dispatched sacrifice at the tomb of Nüwa; visiting Shaan, he dispatched sacrifice at all tombs along the route—only for Wen and Wu of Zhou did the prayer text bear the imperial name, in honor of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, on a western tour, he sent offerings at Nüwa's tomb; visiting Shaanxi, he sent offerings at every tomb along the route—only for King Wen and King Wu of Zhou did the prayer bear the imperial name, in honor of the sages.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，遺諭，言：「明太祖起布衣，統方夏，駕軼漢、唐、宋諸君。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, in a testamentary instruction, he said: "Ming Taizu rose from common cloth and unified the realm, surpassing the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixty-first year Kangxi left instructions: "Ming Taizu rose from common origins and unified the realm, surpassing the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song.

sentences.zh: 末葉災荒，臣工內訌，寇盜外起，以致社稷顛覆。

translations.literal: In the dynasty's last years came famine and disaster, ministers quarreled within, and bandits rose without, until the altars of state were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: In its last years famine struck, ministers quarreled within, and bandits rose without, until the state fell.

sentences.zh: 考其嗣主，未有荒墜顯跡，蓋亦曆數使然。

translations.literal: Examining his successors, there are no clear traces of dissolute ruin—this too was the working of destiny.
translations.idiomatic: Examining his successors, none show clear signs of dissolute ruin—this too was destiny.

sentences.zh: 且其制度規模，我朝多所依據。

translations.literal: Moreover, in institutions and administrative models our dynasty has drawn heavily upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our dynasty has drawn heavily on Ming institutions and administrative models.

sentences.zh: 允宜甄訪支派，量授爵秩，俾奉春秋饗祀。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to search out their collateral lines, grant titles in due measure, and have them perform spring and autumn offerings."
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to seek out their descendants, grant titles as appropriate, and have them perform spring and autumn offerings."

sentences.zh: 世宗纘緒，遂授硃之璉一等侯世襲，往江寧、昌平致祭，自是歲舉以為常。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the succession, he granted Zhu Zhilian the hereditary rank of first-class marquis and sent him to offer sacrifice at Jiangning and Changping; thereafter this was performed annually as a regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng succeeded him, he granted Zhu Zhilian a hereditary first-class marquisate and sent him to sacrifice at Jiangning and Changping; thereafter this was performed annually.

sentences.zh: 帝堯陵向有二：一在平陽，一在濮州。

translations.literal: The tomb of Emperor Yao had long been said to exist in two places: one at Pingyang, one at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao's tomb had long been identified in two places: at Pingyang and at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 濮州東南穀林，古雷澤也。

translations.literal: Gulin southeast of Puzhou was the ancient Lei Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Gulin southeast of Puzhou was the ancient Lei Marsh.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，修葺釐正，定穀林為舊址，平陽時奠如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, repairs and corrections were made, Gulin was fixed as the original site, and seasonal offerings at Pingyang continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's first year repairs were made, Gulin was confirmed as the original site, and seasonal offerings at Pingyang continued as before.

sentences.zh: 並修神農、虞舜陵廟，置陵戶典守。

translations.literal: The tombs and temples of Shennong and Shun were also repaired, and tomb households were established to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The tombs and temples of Shennong and Shun were also repaired, and tomb households were appointed to guard them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以陝西古建都地，帝王陵墓多，命疆吏考其不載會典者，所在令有司防護。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, because Shaanxi was an ancient capital region with many imperial tombs, frontier officials were ordered to investigate those not recorded in the Collected Statutes and have local authorities protect them wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, because Shaanxi was an ancient capital region with many imperial tombs, frontier officials were ordered to investigate tombs not listed in the Collected Statutes and have local authorities protect them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕幸曲阜，奠少昊陵，嗣是東巡皆躬祭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the imperial carriage visited Qufu and offered at the tomb of Shaohao; thereafter on every eastern tour he sacrificed in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Qianlong visited Qufu and offered at Shaohao's tomb; thereafter on every eastern tour he sacrificed in person.

sentences.zh: 十六年，選姒氏子姓一人，授世襲八品官，奉祀禹陵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, one descendant of the Si clan was selected and granted a hereditary eighth-rank office to maintain sacrifice at the tomb of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year a descendant of the Si clan was granted a hereditary eighth-rank office to maintain sacrifice at Yu's tomb.

sentences.zh: 趙城女媧陵，廟中故有塑像，帝斥其黷慢，徹之，改立神位，禁私禱。

translations.literal: At the tomb of Nüwa in Zhaocheng, the temple had formerly held a sculpted image; the emperor condemned this as irreverent, removed it, replaced it with a spirit tablet, and forbade private prayer.
translations.idiomatic: At Nüwa's tomb in Zhaocheng the temple had held a sculpted image; Qianlong condemned this as irreverent, removed it, installed a spirit tablet, and forbade private prayer.

sentences.zh: 十八年，謁泰陵，禮畢，詣房山祭金太祖陵，賚其裔完顏氏官爵、幣帛。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, after visiting the Tailing tomb and completing the rites, he proceeded to Fangshan to sacrifice at the tomb of the Jin founding ancestor and bestowed office, rank, and silks on his descendant of the Wanyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, after visiting the Tailing tomb, he went to Fangshan to sacrifice at the Jin founder's tomb and bestowed office, rank, and silks on a Wanyan descendant.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定帝王陵寢與岳鎮海瀆、先師闕里皆遣官行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, it was fixed that sacrifice at imperial tombs, the sacred mountains and rivers, and the First Teacher's temple at Qufu should all be performed by dispatched officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the court fixed that sacrifice at imperial tombs, sacred mountains and rivers, and Confucius's temple at Qufu should all be performed by dispatched officials.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，禮臣言：「堯陵見正史者，兩漢地理志云：『濟陰郡成陽有堯冢靈台。』

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the Board of Rites stated: "References to Yao's tomb in the standard histories include the Geography Monographs of the Two Han, which say: 'Chengyang in Jiyin commandery has Yao's mound and the Spirit Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the Board of Rites reported: "Standard histories place Yao's tomb as the Geography Monographs of the Two Han record: 'Chengyang in Jiyin commandery has Yao's mound and the Spirit Terrace.

sentences.zh: 劉向傳稱『葬濟陰』。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's biography states 'buried in Jiyin.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's biography states he was 'buried in Jiyin.'

sentences.zh: 晉地理志：『成陽舜所漁，堯冢在西。』

translations.literal: The Jin Geography Monograph says: "Chengyang is where Shun fished; Yao's mound is to the west."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Geography Monograph says: "Chengyang is where Shun fished; Yao's mound lies to the west."

sentences.zh: 宋史禮志：『在濮州雷澤東穀林山。』

translations.literal: The Rites Monograph of the Song History says: 'It is at Gulin Mountain east of Lei Marsh in Puzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Monograph of the Song History places it at Gulin Mountain east of Lei Marsh in Puzhou.'

sentences.zh: 呂氏春秋，帝王世紀，水經注所引述征記，括地誌，太平寰宇記，路史，集古錄諸說，皆與正史符。

translations.literal: The accounts in the Lüshi Chunqiu, Diwang Shiji, the Shuzheng Ji cited in the Water Classic Commentary, Kuodi Zhi, Taiping Huanyu Ji, Lu Shi, and Jigu Lu all accord with the standard histories.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts in the Lüshi Chunqiu, Diwang Shiji, the Shuzheng Ji cited in the Water Classic Commentary, Kuodi Zhi, Taiping Huanyu Ji, Lu Shi, and Jigu Lu all agree with the standard histories.

sentences.zh: 後漢元和以來，祀典並於其地行。

translations.literal: From the Yuanhe era of Later Han onward, the sacrificial canon was performed at that site.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuanhe era of Later Han onward, sacrifice was performed at that site.

sentences.zh: 明洪武雖改祀東平，而隸魯境則一。

translations.literal: Although Ming Hongwu shifted worship to Dongping, it remained within the territory of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ming Hongwu shifted worship to Dongping, it remained within the territory of Lu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定穀林為堯陵，稽古正訛，萬世可守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, Gulin was fixed as Yao's tomb—examining antiquity to correct error, a rule to be observed for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianlong, Gulin was confirmed as Yao's tomb—correcting error by examining antiquity, a rule to be observed forever.

sentences.zh: 嗣後祭告，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Thereafter sacrificial announcements followed the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter sacrificial announcements followed the established regulations.

sentences.zh: 其平陽一陵，有司祀之，如東平例。」

translations.literal: As for the tomb at Pingyang, the responsible officials sacrifice there, following the Dongping precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The tomb at Pingyang is maintained by local officials, following the Dongping precedent."

sentences.zh: 已，大理寺卿尹嘉銓請罷明宣宗、世宗二陵祭告，廷議以為：「宣宗有善政，不應以一二事生訾議，唯世宗戮忠親佞，實與史合，應停饗祀。」

translations.literal: Thereafter, the chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review, Yin Jiaquan, requested discontinuing sacrificial announcements at the tombs of Ming Xuanzong and Shizong. Court deliberation held: "Xuanzong had good policies and should not be faulted for one or two matters; only Shizong executed the loyal and favored the sycophantic, which truly accords with history—his offerings should be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Jiaquan of the Court of Judicial Review asked to discontinue sacrificial announcements at the tombs of Ming Xuanzong and Shizong. The court held: "Xuanzong had good policies and should not be faulted for isolated acts; only Shizong executed the loyal and favored sycophants, which history confirms—his offerings should be suspended."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，南巡至江寧，祭明太祖陵，禮臣具儀上，三奠酒，每奠一拜。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, on a southern tour reaching Jiangning, he sacrificed at the tomb of Ming Taizu; the Board of Rites submitted the rite, with three libations of wine and one bow at each libation.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year, on a southern tour to Jiangning, he sacrificed at Ming Taizu's tomb; the Board of Rites proposed three libations with one bow at each.

sentences.zh: 帝命用祀少昊陵例，二跪六拜，不必奠酒，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered use of the rite for Shaohao's tomb: two kneelings and six prostrations, without libations of wine, and this was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong ordered the rite used for Shaohao's tomb: two kneelings and six prostrations, without libations, and this was established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 五十年，幸湯山，道昌平，親酹明成祖陵，繕葺之，仍建定陵饗殿，並復世宗祀事。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, visiting Tangshan and passing through Changping, he personally poured libation at the tomb of Ming Chengzu, repaired it, rebuilt the offering hall at the Dingling tomb, and restored Shizong's sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, visiting Tangshan and passing through Changping, he personally poured libation at Ming Chengzu's tomb, repaired it, rebuilt the offering hall at Dingling, and restored Shizong's sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，罷遣官，敕各省副都統、總兵官舉行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, dispatched officials were discontinued; vice commanders-in-chief and regional commanders of each province were ordered to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing's first year dispatched officials were discontinued; vice commanders-in-chief and regional commanders in each province were ordered to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 九年，謁東陵，道盤山，閱明陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he visited the Eastern Tomb, passed through Pan Mountain, and inspected the Ming tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he visited the Eastern Tomb, passed through Pan Mountain, and inspected the Ming tombs.

sentences.zh: 故事，往長陵奠醊，遣王大臣致奠餘陵。

translations.literal: By precedent, libation was poured at the Changling tomb while princes and senior ministers were dispatched to offer at the remaining tombs.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent libation was poured at Changling while princes and senior ministers were sent to the other tombs.

sentences.zh: 是日仁宗躬詣，三奠畢，乃三拜。

translations.literal: On that day Renzong went in person; after three libations were completed, he performed three bows.
translations.idiomatic: That day Renzong went in person; after three libations he bowed three times.

sentences.zh: 望祭元太祖、世祖陵，向在德勝門外，位暢春園、圓明園南，帝以為乖制。

translations.literal: Distant sacrifice at the tombs of the Yuan founding ancestor and Shizu had formerly been performed outside Desheng Gate, south of the Changchun and Yuanming gardens; the emperor held this contrary to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Distant sacrifice at the Yuan founders' tombs had been performed outside Desheng Gate, south of the Changchun and Yuanming gardens; the emperor held this improper.

sentences.zh: 命嗣後行慶典，改於清河以北、昌平以南擇地行禮。

translations.literal: He ordered that thereafter, when great celebrations were performed, a site should be chosen north of the Qing River and south of Changping for the rite.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that thereafter, on great celebrations, the rite should be performed at a site chosen north of the Qing River and south of Changping.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年，定明陵春秋致祭，由襲侯往行，餘以其族官品峻者攝之，或遣散秩大臣，為永制。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang, spring and autumn sacrifice at the Ming tombs was fixed: the hereditary marquis should perform it, the remaining tombs should be attended by the highest-ranking member of the clan, or a minister without regular portfolio might be dispatched—established as permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's sixteenth year spring and autumn sacrifice at the Ming tombs was fixed: the hereditary marquis performed at the main tombs, others by the highest-ranking clan member or a dispatched minister without portfolio—as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，諭禁開墾明陵旁近地畝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, an edict forbade opening and cultivating land near the Ming tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu's seventh year an edict forbade cultivating land near the Ming tombs.

sentences.zh: 傳心殿順治十四年，沿明制舉經筵，祭先師孔子弘德殿。

translations.literal: Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, following the Ming system, the Classics Lectern was held and the First Teacher Confucius was worshipped in the Hongde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind: In Shunzhi's fourteenth year, following Ming practice, the Classics Lectern was held and Confucius was worshipped in the Hongde Hall.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年續舉，遣官告祭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi it was resumed, and officials were dispatched to announce the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's tenth year it was resumed, with officials dispatched to announce the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，規建傳心殿，位文華殿東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind was planned and built east of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind was built east of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 正中祀皇師伏羲、神農、軒轅，帝師堯、舜，王師禹、湯、文、武，南鄉。

translations.literal: At the center were worshipped, facing south, the imperial teachers Fuxi, Shennong, and Xuanyuan; the royal teachers Yao and Shun; and the kingly teachers Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the center, facing south, were worshipped the imperial teachers Fuxi, Shennong, and Xuanyuan; the royal teachers Yao and Shun; and the kingly teachers Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu.

sentences.zh: 東周公，西孔子。

translations.literal: To the east was the Duke of Zhou; to the west, Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou stood to the east; Confucius to the west.

sentences.zh: 祭器視帝王廟。

translations.literal: Ritual vessels followed those of the Temple of Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual vessels followed those of the Temple of Emperors.

sentences.zh: 歲御經筵，前期遣大學士祗告。

translations.literal: Each year when the Classics Lectern was held, a grand secretary was beforehand dispatched to announce reverently.
translations.idiomatic: Each year before the Classics Lectern, a grand secretary was dispatched to announce the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祭傳心殿自此始。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at the Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind began from this time.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝將御經筵，詔言：「先聖、先師，傳道垂統，炳若日星。

translations.literal: The following year, when the emperor was about to preside at the Classics Lectern, an edict stated: "The former sages and former teachers transmitted the Way and handed down the succession, bright as sun and stars.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, before presiding at the Classics Lectern, Kangxi decreed: "The former sages and teachers transmitted the Way and handed down the succession, bright as sun and stars.

sentences.zh: 朕遠承心學，效法不已，漸近自然。

translations.literal: I far inherit the learning of the heart-mind and emulate without ceasing, gradually approaching what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: I inherit their heart-mind learning and emulate them without ceasing, gradually approaching what is natural.

sentences.zh: 施之政教，庶不與聖賢相悖，其躬詣行禮。」

translations.literal: Applying this to government and instruction, I hope not to contradict the sages and worthies—let me go in person to perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: In applying this to government and instruction, I hope not to contradict the sages—let me perform the rite in person."

sentences.zh: 祀日具香燭，鉶一，籩、豆各二，奠帛、爵，讀祝，以祭。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, incense and candles were prepared, one meat vessel, two platters and two cups each, silk and libation cups were presented, the prayer was read, and sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice incense and candles were prepared, with one meat vessel and two platters and cups each; silk and libation cups were presented, the prayer read, and sacrifice performed.

sentences.zh: 帝御袞服，行二跪六拜禮。

translations.literal: The emperor wore ceremonial robes and performed the rite of two kneelings and six prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore ceremonial robes and performed two kneelings and six prostrations.

sentences.zh: 太子春秋會講，亦先祭告焉。

translations.literal: When the crown prince held spring and autumn lectures, he likewise first announced sacrifice there.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince held spring and autumn lectures, he likewise announced sacrifice there first.

sentences.zh: 月朔望遣太常卿供酒果上香。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of each month the minister of rites was dispatched to supply wine and fruit and offer incense.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month the minister of rites supplied wine and fruit and offered incense.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，定本日行祗告禮，自是以為常。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, it was fixed that the reverent announcement rite should be performed on the same day, and this became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng's fourth year the reverent announcement was fixed for the same day, and this became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，親祭傳心殿，六十年歸政，再行之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong, he sacrificed in person at the Hall for Transmitting the Heart-Mind; when he abdicated in the sixtieth year, he performed it again.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's sixth year he sacrificed in person at the hall; when he abdicated in his sixtieth year, he did so again.

sentences.zh: 歷仁宗、宣宗、文宗，並親詣祗告，後不復行。

translations.literal: Through Renzong, Xuanzong, and Wenzong, each went in person to announce reverently; afterward the practice was not resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, Xuanzong, and Wenzong each went in person; afterward the practice lapsed.

sentences.zh: 經筵儀制，別詳嘉禮。

translations.literal: The ritual regulations for the Classics Lectern are detailed separately under Auspicious Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual regulations for the Classics Lectern are detailed separately under Auspicious Rites.

sentences.zh: 至聖先師孔子崇德元年，建廟盛京，遣大學士范文程致祭。

translations.literal: The Most Sage First Teacher Confucius: In the first year of Chongde, a temple was built in Mukden, and Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng was dispatched to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Most Sage First Teacher Confucius: In Chongde's first year a temple was built in Mukden, and Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng was sent to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 奉顏子、曾子、子思、孟子配。

translations.literal: Yanzi, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius were installed as associates.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mencius were installed as associates.

sentences.zh: 定春秋二仲上丁行釋奠禮。

translations.literal: It was fixed that the libation and offering rite should be performed on the first ding day of the second month of spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The libation and offering rite was fixed for the first ding day of the second month of spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 世祖定大原，以京師國子監為大學，立文廟。

translations.literal: When Shizu secured Taiyuan, he made the Directorate of Education in the capital the Grand Academy and established a Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu secured Taiyuan, he made the capital Directorate of Education the Grand Academy and established a Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 制方，南鄉。

translations.literal: It was built square, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: It was built square, facing south.

sentences.zh: 西持敬門，西鄉。

translations.literal: To the west was the Gate of Reverent Attention, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was the Gate of Reverent Attention, facing west.

sentences.zh: 前大成門，內列戟二十四，石鼓十，東西舍各十一楹，北鄉。

translations.literal: In front was the Dacheng Gate; within were displayed twenty-four halberds and ten stone drums; east and west lodges each had eleven bays, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In front was the Dacheng Gate; within were twenty-four halberds and ten stone drums; east and west lodges each had eleven bays, facing north.

sentences.zh: 大成殿七楹，陛三出，兩廡各十九楹，東西列舍如門內，南鄉。

translations.literal: The Dacheng Hall had seven bays, with three flights of steps; the two side halls each had nineteen bays; east and west rows of lodges like those within the gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Dacheng Hall had seven bays with three flights of steps; the two side halls each had nineteen bays; east and west rows of lodges like those within the gate, all facing south.

sentences.zh: 啟聖祠正殿五楹，兩廡各三楹，燎爐、瘞坎、神庫、神廚、宰牲亭、井亭皆如制。

translations.literal: The Qisheng Shrine main hall had five bays, the two side halls three bays each; offering furnaces, burial pits, spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, slaughter pavilion, and well pavilion were all as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The Qisheng Shrine main hall had five bays and the side halls three each; offering furnaces, burial pits, spirit storehouse, spirit kitchen, slaughter pavilion, and well pavilion were all as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，定稱大成至聖文宣先師孔子，春秋上丁，遣大學士一人行祭，翰林官二人分獻，祭酒祭啟聖祠，以先賢、先儒配饗從祀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he was titled the Most Sage First Teacher Confucius, Great Completion, Literary Propagation. On the upper ding days of spring and autumn, one grand secretary was dispatched to sacrifice, two Hanlin officials to distribute offerings, and the chancellor of the Directorate to sacrifice at the Qisheng Shrine, with former worthies and former scholars as associates and attendant worship.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi's second year he was titled the Most Sage First Teacher Confucius, Great Completion, Literary Propagation. On the upper ding days of spring and autumn one grand secretary sacrificed, two Hanlin officials distributed offerings, and the chancellor sacrificed at the Qisheng Shrine, with former worthies and scholars as associates and attendants.

sentences.zh: 有故，改用次丁或下丁。

translations.literal: If there was cause, the second or third ding day was used instead.
translations.idiomatic: If necessary, the second or third ding day was used instead.

sentences.zh: 月朔，祭酒釋菜，設酒、芹、棗、栗。

translations.literal: On the first of the month, the chancellor performed the vegetable libation, setting out wine, celery, dates, and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the month the chancellor performed the vegetable libation with wine, celery, dates, and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 先師四配三獻，十哲兩廡，監丞等分獻。

translations.literal: The First Teacher and four associates received three offerings; the Ten Wise Ones and the two side halls were distributed by the director, vice-director, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The First Teacher and four associates received three offerings; the Ten Wise Ones and side halls were served by the director, vice-director, and others.

sentences.zh: 望日，司業上香。

translations.literal: On the full moon, the vice-chancellor offered incense.
translations.idiomatic: On the full moon the vice-chancellor offered incense.

sentences.zh: 正中祀先師孔子，南鄉。

translations.literal: At the center the First Teacher Confucius was worshipped, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At the center the First Teacher Confucius was worshipped, facing south.

sentences.zh: 四配：復聖顏子，宗聖曾子，述聖子思子，亞聖孟子。

translations.literal: The four associates: Yanzi, Sage of Restoration; Zengzi, Sage of Transmission; Zisi, Sage of Exposition; and Mencius, Sage Second to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The four associates: Yan Hui, Sage of Restoration; Zeng Shen, Sage of Transmission; Zisi, Sage of Exposition; and Mencius, Sage Second to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 十哲：閔子損、冉子雍、端木子賜、仲子由、卜子商、冉子耕、宰子予、冉子求、言子偃、顓孫子師，俱東西鄉。

translations.literal: The Ten Wise Ones: Minzi Sun, Ranzi Yong, Duanmuzi Ci, Zhongzi You, Bozi Shang, Ranzi Geng, Zaizi Yu, Ranzi Qiu, Yanzi Yan, and Zhuansunzi Shi—all facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Wise Ones: Min Sun, Ran Yong, Duanmu Ci, Zhong You, Bu Shang, Ran Geng, Zai Yu, Ran Qiu, Yan Yan, and Zhuansun Shi—all facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 西廡從祀：先賢澹臺滅明、宓不齊、原憲、公冶長、南宮适、公晳哀、商瞿、高柴、漆雕開、樊須、司馬耕、商澤、有若、梁鱣、巫馬施、冉孺、顏辛、伯虔、曹䘏、冉季、公孫龍、漆雕徒文、秦商、漆雕哆、顏高、公西赤、壤駟赤、任不齊、石作蜀、公良孺、公夏首、公肩定、後處、鄡單、奚容蒧、罕父黑、顏祖、榮旗、句井疆、左人郢、秦祖、鄭國、縣成、原亢、公祖句茲、廉潔、燕伋、叔仲會、樂欬、公西輿如、狄黑、邽巽、孔忠、陳亢、公西蒧、琴張、顏之仆、步叔乘、施之常、秦非、申棖、顏噲、左丘明、周敦頤、張載、程顥、程頤、邵雍、硃熹，凡六十九人；

translations.literal: Attendant worship in the west side hall: former worthies Tantai Mieming, Mi Buqi, Yuan Xian, Gongye Chang, Nangong Kuo, Gongxi Ai, Shang Qu, Gao Chai, Qidiao Kai, Fan Xu, Sima Niu, Shang Ze, You Ruo, Liang Zhan, Wuma Shi, Ran Ru, Yan Xin, Bo Qian, Cao Xu, Ran Ji, Gongsun Long, Qidiao Tuweng, Qin Shang, Qidiao Duo, Yan Gao, Gongxi Chi, Xiangsi Chi, Ren Buqi, Shizuo Shu, Gongliang Ru, Gongxia Shou, Gongjian Ding, Hou Chu, Qiu Dan, Xi Rong Dian, Hanfu Hei, Yan Zu, Rong Qi, Gou Jingjiang, Zuoren Ying, Qin Zu, Zheng Guo, Xian Cheng, Yuan Kang, Gongzu Gouzi, Lian Jie, Yan Ji, Shuzhong Hui, Yue Xin, Gongxi Yuru, Di Hei, Gui Xun, Kong Zhong, Chen Kang, Gongxi Dian, Qin Zhang, Yan Zhipu, Bushu Cheng, Shi Zhichang, Qin Fei, Shen Cheng, Yan Kuai, Zuoqiu Ming, Zhou Dunyi, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Shao Yong, and Zhu Xi—in all sixty-nine persons;
translations.idiomatic: The west side hall enshrined sixty-nine former worthies, from Tantai Mieming and Mi Buqi through Confucius's disciples to Zuoqiu Ming, Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Shao Yong, and Zhu Xi;

sentences.zh: 先儒公羊高、穀梁赤、伏勝、孔安國、毛萇、後蒼、高堂生、董仲舒、王通、杜子春、韓愈、司馬光、歐陽修、胡安國、楊時、呂祖謙、羅從彥、蔡沈、李侗、陸九淵、張栻、許衡、真德秀、王守仁、陳獻章、薛瑄、胡居仁，凡二十八人。

translations.literal: former scholars Gongyang Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Kong Anguo, Mao Chang, Hou Cang, Gaotang Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Wang Tong, Du Zichun, Han Yu, Sima Guang, Ouyang Xiu, Hu Anguo, Yang Shi, Lü Zuqian, Luo Congyan, Cai Shen, Li Tong, Lu Jiuyuan, Zhang Shi, Xu Heng, Zhen Dexiu, Wang Shouren, Chen Xianzhang, Xue Xuan, and Hu Juren—in all twenty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty-eight former scholars including Gongyang Gao, Guliang Chi, Fu Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Han Yu, Sima Guang, Ouyang Xiu, Zhu Xi's teachers and peers, Wang Yangming, and Hu Juren.

sentences.zh: 啟聖祠，啟聖公位正中，南鄉。

translations.literal: In the Qisheng Shrine, Lord Qisheng stood at the center, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qisheng Shrine, Lord Qisheng stood at the center, facing south.

sentences.zh: 配位：先賢顏無繇、曾點、孔鯉、孟孫氏，東西鄉。

translations.literal: Associates: former worthies Yan Wuyao, Zeng Dian, Kong Li, and Mengsun Shi, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Associates: Yan Wuyao, Zeng Dian, Kong Li, and Mengsun Shi, facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 兩廡從祀：先儒周輔成、程、蔡元定、硃松。

translations.literal: Attendant worship in the two side halls: former scholars Zhou Fucheng, the Cheng family, Cai Yuanding, and Zhu Song.
translations.idiomatic: The side halls enshrined Zhou Fucheng, the Cheng family, Cai Yuanding, and Zhu Song.

sentences.zh: 九年，世祖視學，釋奠先師，王、公、百官，齋戒陪祀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shizu inspected the academy and performed the libation and offering to the First Teacher; princes, dukes, and all officials fasted and attended as accompanying sacrificers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Shizu inspected the academy and performed the libation to the First Teacher; princes, dukes, and officials fasted and attended.

sentences.zh: 前期，衍聖公率孔、顏、曾、孟、仲五氏世襲五經博士，孔氏族五人，顏、曾、孟、仲族各二人，赴都。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Duke of Yansheng led the hereditary Five Classics doctors of the Kong, Yan, Zeng, Meng, and Zhong clans—five from the Kong clan, two each from the Yan, Zeng, Meng, and Zhong clans—to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Duke of Yansheng led the hereditary Five Classics doctors of the Kong, Yan, Zeng, Meng, and Zhong clans—five Kongs, two each from the other four—to the capital.

sentences.zh: 暨五氏子孫居京秩者咸與祭。

translations.literal: Together with descendants of the five clans holding office in the capital, all participated in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the five clans holding office in the capital also participated.

sentences.zh: 是歲授孔氏南宗博士一人，奉西安祀。

translations.literal: That year one doctor of the Southern Branch of the Kong clan was appointed to maintain sacrifice at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: That year a doctor of the Southern Branch of the Kong clan was appointed to maintain sacrifice at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 十四年，給事中張文光言：「追王固誣聖，而『大成文宣』四字，亦不足以盡聖，宜改題『至聖先師』。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang stated: "Posthumous ennoblement as king is indeed slander of the sage, and the four characters 'Great Completion, Literary Propagation' are also insufficient to exhaust his sanctity—it is fitting to change the title to 'Most Sage First Teacher.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang argued: "Posthumous kingship slanders the sage, and 'Great Completion, Literary Propagation' cannot exhaust his sanctity—the title should be 'Most Sage First Teacher.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，頒太學中和韶樂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, the Zhonghe Shaoyue music was issued to the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's sixth year the Zhonghe Shaoyue music was issued to the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，御書「萬世師表」額懸大成殿，並頒直省學宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the imperial inscription "Model Teacher for Ten Thousand Generations" was hung in the Dacheng Hall and issued to provincial academies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the imperial inscription "Model Teacher for Ten Thousand Generations" was hung in the Dacheng Hall and issued to provincial academies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，御制孔子贊序、顏曾思孟四贊鑱之石。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the imperially composed Preface to the Eulogy of Confucius and four eulogies for Yan, Zeng, Si, and Meng were carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the imperially composed Preface to the Eulogy of Confucius and four eulogies for Yan, Zeng, Si, and Meng were carved on stone.

sentences.zh: 揭其文頒直省。

translations.literal: The texts were posted and issued to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The texts were posted and issued to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，以硃子昌明聖學，升躋十哲，位次卜子。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, because Master Zhu had clarified sagely learning, he was elevated to the Ten Wise Ones, ranking after Bozi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year Zhu Xi was elevated to the Ten Wise Ones, ranking after Bu Shang, for clarifying sagely learning.

sentences.zh: 尋命宋儒范仲淹從祀。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the Song scholar Fan Zhongyan was ordered to attendant worship.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Fan Zhongyan was added to attendant worship.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔追封孔子五代王爵，於是錫木金父公曰肇聖，祈父公曰裕聖，防叔公曰詒聖，伯夏公曰昌聖，叔梁公曰啟聖，更啟聖祠曰崇聖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, an edict posthumously ennobled five generations of Confucius's ancestors as kings: Shujin Fugong as Lord Zhaosheng, Qifu as Lord Yusheng, Fangshu as Lord Yisheng, Bo Xia as Lord Changsheng, and Shuliang as Lord Qisheng; the Qisheng Shrine was renamed Chongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng's first year an edict posthumously ennobled five generations of Confucius's ancestors, renamed the Qisheng Shrine Chongsheng, and titled Shuliang Lord Qisheng.

sentences.zh: 肇聖位中，裕聖左，詒聖右，昌聖次左，啟聖次右，俱南鄉。

translations.literal: Lord Zhaosheng stood at the center; Lord Yusheng to the left, Lord Yisheng to the right; Lord Changsheng next left, Lord Qisheng next right—all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zhaosheng stood at the center; Lord Yusheng to the left, Lord Yisheng to the right; Lord Changsheng next left, Lord Qisheng next right—all facing south.

sentences.zh: 配饗從祀如故。

translations.literal: Associates and attendant worship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Associates and attendant worship remained as before.

sentences.zh: 二年，視學釋奠，世宗以祔饗廟庭諸賢，有先罷宜復，或舊闕宜增，與孰應祔祀崇聖祠者，命廷臣考議。

translations.literal: In the second year, inspecting the academy and performing the libation, Shizong held that among the worthies enshrined in the temple court, some previously removed should be restored, some old omissions should be added, and some should be enshrined in the Chongsheng Shrine—he ordered the court to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, inspecting the academy, Yongzheng ordered the court to deliberate which worthies removed from the temple should be restored, which omitted names should be added, and who should enter the Chongsheng Shrine.

sentences.zh: 議上，帝曰：「戴聖、何休非純儒，鄭眾、盧植、服虔、范甯守一家言，視鄭康成淳質深通者有間，其他諸儒是否允協，應再確議。」

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor said: "Dai Sheng and He Xiu were not pure Confucians; Zheng Zhong, Lu Zhi, Fu Qian, and Fan Ning adhered to one school's doctrine and fall short of Zheng Xuan's plain sincerity and deep mastery—whether the other scholars are fitting should be deliberated again with certainty."
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor said: "Dai Sheng and He Xiu were not pure Confucians; Zheng Zhong, Lu Zhi, Fu Qian, and Fan Ning held to one school and fall short of Zheng Xuan—whether the others are fitting must be deliberated again."

sentences.zh: 復議上。

translations.literal: A revised deliberation was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A revised deliberation was submitted.

sentences.zh: 於是復祀者六人：曰林放、蘧瑗、秦冉、顏何、鄭康成、范甯。

translations.literal: Thereupon six were restored to worship: Lin Fang, Qu Yuan, Qin Ran, Yan He, Zheng Xuan, and Fan Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Six were restored: Lin Fang, Qu Yuan, Qin Ran, Yan He, Zheng Xuan, and Fan Ning.

sentences.zh: 增祀者二十人：曰孔子弟子縣亶、牧皮，孟子弟子樂正子、公都子、萬章、公孫丑，漢諸葛亮，宋尹焞、魏了翁、黃幹、陳淳、何基、王柏、趙復，元金履祥、許謙、陳澔，明羅欽順、蔡清，國朝陸隴其。

translations.literal: Twenty were added: Confucius's disciples Xian Xi and Mu Pi; Mencius's disciples Master Yuezheng, Gongduzi, Wan Zhang, and Gongsun Chou; Han Zhuge Liang; Song Yin Tun, Wei Liaoweng, Huang Gan, Chen Chun, He Ji, Wang Bai, and Zhao Fu; Yuan Jin Lüxiang, Xu Qian, and Chen Hao; Ming Luo Qinshun and Cai Qing; and our dynasty's Lu Longqi.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty were added: Confucius's disciples Xian Xi and Mu Pi; Mencius's disciples Yuezheng, Gongdu, Wan Zhang, and Gongsun Chou; Zhuge Liang; Song scholars Yin Tun through Zhao Fu; Yuan Jin Lüxiang, Xu Qian, and Chen Hao; Ming Luo Qinshun and Cai Qing; and Lu Longqi of our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 入崇聖祠者一人，宋橫渠張子迪。

translations.literal: One entered the Chongsheng Shrine: Song Hengqu Zhang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: One entered the Chongsheng Shrine: Zhang Zai of Hengqu.

sentences.zh: 尋命避先師諱，加「邑」為「邱」，地名讀如期音，惟「圜丘」字不改。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter it was ordered to avoid the First Teacher's taboo name: add "yi" to make "Qiu," place names to be read like the word for "period," only the character for "round mound" was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter taboo avoidance was ordered: add "yi" to make "Qiu," read place names like "period," except the character for "round mound."

sentences.zh: 四年八月仲丁，世宗親詣釋奠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the mid-ding day of the eighth month, Shizong went in person to perform the libation and offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the mid-ding day of the eighth month, Yongzheng performed the libation in person.

sentences.zh: 初，春秋二祀無親祭制，至是始定。

translations.literal: Initially there was no regulation for personal sacrifice at the two spring and autumn observances; from this time it was first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously there was no personal sacrifice at the spring and autumn observances; from this time it was established.

sentences.zh: 犧牲、籩豆視丁祭，行禮二跪六拜，奠帛獻爵，改立為跪，仍讀祝，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: Victims and platters followed the ding-day sacrifice; the rite was two kneelings and six prostrations, presenting silk and libation cups—standing was changed to kneeling, the prayer was still read, but wine of blessing and sacrificial meat were not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Victims and platters followed the ding-day sacrifice; the rite was two kneelings and six prostrations with silk and libation cups—kneeling replaced standing, the prayer was read, but blessing wine and sacrificial meat were not taken.

sentences.zh: 尚書分獻四配，侍郎分獻十一哲兩廡。

translations.literal: Ministers distributed offerings to the four associates; vice-ministers to the eleven wise ones and two side halls.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers distributed offerings to the four associates; vice-ministers to the eleven wise ones and side halls.

sentences.zh: 明年，定八月二十七日先師誕辰，官民軍士，致齋一日，以為常。

translations.literal: The following year, the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month was fixed as the First Teacher's birthday; officials, commoners, and soldiers were to fast one day—established as regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the twenty-seventh of the eighth month was fixed as the First Teacher's birthday; officials, commoners, and soldiers fasted one day—as regular practice.

sentences.zh: 又明年，御書「生民未有」額，頒懸如故事。

translations.literal: The year after, the imperial inscription "Never Before Among the People" was issued and hung according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, the imperial inscription "Never Before Among the People" was issued and hung as before.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定親祭儀，香案前三上香。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the personal sacrifice rite was fixed: three offerings of incense before the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the personal sacrifice rite was fixed: three offerings of incense before the incense table.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，諭易大成殿及門黃瓦，崇聖祠綠瓦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, an edict ordered yellow tiles for the Dacheng Hall and gate, green tiles for the Chongsheng Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's second year yellow tiles were ordered for the Dacheng Hall and gate, green for the Chongsheng Shrine.

sentences.zh: 復元儒吳澄祀。

translations.literal: Worship of the Yuan scholar Wu Cheng was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Worship of the Yuan scholar Wu Cheng was restored.

sentences.zh: 三年，升有子若為十二哲，位次卜子商。

translations.literal: In the third year, You Ruo was elevated to the Twelve Wise Ones, ranking after Bozi Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year You Ruo was elevated to the Twelve Wise Ones, ranking after Bu Shang.

sentences.zh: 移硃子次顓孫子師。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi was moved to rank after Zhuansunzi Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi was moved to rank after Zhuansun Shi.

sentences.zh: 是歲上丁，帝親視學釋奠，嚴駕出，至廟門外降輿。

translations.literal: That year on the upper ding day, the emperor personally inspected the academy and performed the libation; with full escort he issued forth and alighted outside the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: That upper ding day Qianlong inspected the academy and performed the libation in person, alighting outside the temple gate with full escort.

sentences.zh: 入中門，俟大次，出盥訖，入大成中門，升階，三上香，行二跪六拜禮。

translations.literal: He entered the middle gate, waited in the great curtained enclosure, emerged after ablutions, entered the middle Dacheng gate, ascended the steps, offered incense three times, and performed two kneelings and six prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the middle gate, waited in the great enclosure, washed, entered the middle Dacheng gate, ascended the steps, offered incense three times, and performed two kneelings and six prostrations.

sentences.zh: 有司以次奠獻。

translations.literal: Officials presented offerings in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Officials presented offerings in sequence.

sentences.zh: 正殿，分獻官升東、西階，入左、右門，詣四配、十二哲位前，兩廡分獻官分詣先賢、先儒位前，上香奠獻畢，帝三拜，亞獻、終獻如初。

translations.literal: In the main hall, distributing officers ascended the east and west steps, entered the left and right gates, and proceeded before the four associates and twelve wise ones; side-hall officers proceeded before the former worthies and scholars; when incense and offerings were complete, the emperor bowed three times; secondary and final offerings followed as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall distributing officers ascended the east and west steps to the four associates and twelve wise ones; side-hall officers to the former worthies and scholars; when offerings were complete the emperor bowed three times; secondary and final offerings followed.

sentences.zh: 釋奠用三獻始此。

translations.literal: The use of three offerings at the libation and offering rite began here.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings at the libation rite began here.

sentences.zh: 其祭崇聖祠，拜位在階下，承祭官升東階，入左門，詣肇聖王位前上香畢，分獻官升東、西階，入左、右門，分詣配位及兩廡從位前上香，三跪九拜。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the Chongsheng Shrine: the place of bowing was below the steps; the presiding officer ascended the east steps, entered the left gate, and offered incense before Lord Zhaosheng; distributing officers ascended east and west steps, entered left and right gates, and offered incense before associates and attendant places in the side halls—three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: At the Chongsheng Shrine the emperor bowed below the steps; the presiding officer offered incense before Lord Zhaosheng; distributing officers before associates and attendants in the side halls—all with three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 奠帛、讀祝，初獻時行。

translations.literal: Presenting silk and reading the prayer were performed at the initial offering.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and the prayer were presented at the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 凡三獻，禮畢。

translations.literal: Three offerings in all; the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings in all; the rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 自是為恆式。

translations.literal: From this it became the constant form.
translations.idiomatic: This became the standard form.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改正太學丁祭牲品，依闕里例用少牢，十二哲東西各一案，兩廡各三案。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, victims for the Grand Academy ding-day sacrifice were corrected: following the Qufu precedent, the xiao lao offering was used; the twelve wise ones had one table each east and west; the two side halls three tables each.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Grand Academy ding-day victims were corrected to the xiao lao offering per Qufu: one table each for the twelve wise ones east and west, three tables each for the side halls.

sentences.zh: 崇聖祠四配，兩廡東西各一案，十二哲位各一帛，東西共二篚。

translations.literal: In the Chongsheng Shrine the four associates and east and west side halls each had one table; each of the twelve wise ones one piece of silk, two baskets east and west together.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongsheng Shrine the four associates and side halls each had one table; each wise one one piece of silk, two baskets east and west.

sentences.zh: 其分獻，正殿東西，翰林官各奠三爵；

translations.literal: For distribution: in the main hall east and west, Hanlin officials each presented three libations;
translations.idiomatic: For distribution: in the main hall Hanlin officials each presented three libations;

sentences.zh: 西廡國子監四人，共奠三爵；

translations.literal: in the west side hall four from the Directorate, three libations together;
translations.idiomatic: in the west side hall four from the Directorate, three libations together;

sentences.zh: 十二哲兩廡奉爵用肄業諸生。

translations.literal: for the twelve wise ones and two side halls, students in training presented the libation cups.
translations.idiomatic: for the twelve wise ones and side halls, students in training presented the cups.

sentences.zh: 定兩廡位序，按史傳年代先後之。

translations.literal: The order of places in the two side halls was fixed according to chronological sequence in historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Side-hall seating was ordered by chronological sequence in historical records.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，葺文廟成，增大門「先師廟」額，正殿及門曰「大成」，帝親書榜，制碑記。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, when repairs to the Confucian temple were complete, the main gate was given the plaque "Temple of the First Teacher"; the main hall and gate were titled "Great Completion"; the emperor personally wrote the boards and composed a stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, when temple repairs were complete, the main gate was titled "Temple of the First Teacher" and the hall "Great Completion"; Qianlong wrote the boards and composed a stele inscription.

sentences.zh: 選內府尊彝中十器，凡犧尊、雷文壺、子爵、內言卣、康侯爵、鼎盟簋、雷紋觚、召仲簋、素洗、犧首罍各一，頒之成均。
