translations.literal: Ten vessels were selected from the imperial ritual bronzes: one each of sacrificial zun, thunder-pattern hu, zi jue, neiyan you, Kanghou jue, dingmeng gui, thunder-pattern gu, Zhaozhong gui, plain basin, and sacrificial-head lei—issued to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Ten ritual bronzes were selected from the imperial collection—sacrificial zun, thunder-pattern hu, zi jue, and seven others—and issued to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 五十年，新建辟雍成，親臨講學，釋奠如故。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, when the new Biyong was complete, he personally attended the lecture and performed the libation as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, when the new Biyong was complete, he lectured in person and performed the libation as before.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，兩舉臨雍儀。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, the ceremony of attending the Biyong was performed twice.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing the Biyong ceremony was performed twice.

sentences.zh: 道光二年詔劉宗周，三年湯斌，五年黃道周，六年陸贄、呂坤，八年孫奇逢，從祀先儒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, Liu Zongzhou was decreed; in the third year Tang Bin; in the fifth year Huang Daozhou; in the sixth year Lu Zhi and Lü Kun; in the eighth year Sun Qifeng—all admitted to secondary worship among earlier Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's second year Liu Zongzhou, in the third Tang Bin, in the fifth Huang Daozhou, in the sixth Lu Zhi and Lü Kun, and in the eighth Sun Qifeng were all admitted to secondary worship among earlier Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 八年，湖北學政王贈芳請祀陳良，帝以言行無可考，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Wang Zengfang, educational commissioner of Hubei, requested worship of Chen Liang; the emperor held that his words and conduct could not be verified, and shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Hubei educational commissioner Wang Zengfang requested worship of Chen Liang; the emperor held his words and conduct unverifiable and shelved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，御史牛鑒以李顒請，部議謂然，帝斥之。

translations.literal: Before long, censor Niu Jian requested Li Yong; the board agreed, but the emperor rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, censor Niu Jian petitioned for Li Yong; the board agreed, but the emperor rejected the request.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔祀孔子不得與佛、老同廟。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict decreed that worship of Confucius must not share a temple with Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict forbade worshipping Confucius in the same temple as Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 是後復以宋臣文天祥、宋儒謝良佐侑饗雲。

translations.literal: After this, the Song minister Wen Tianxiang and the Song Confucian Xie Liangzuo were again added as secondary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Song minister Wen Tianxiang and Song Confucian Xie Liangzuo were again added as secondary offerings.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，增先賢公明儀，宋臣李綱、韓琦侑饗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, the earlier sage Gongming Yi was added, and the Song ministers Li Gang and Han Qi were added as secondary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianfeng the earlier sage Gongming Yi was added, along with Song ministers Li Gang and Han Qi as secondary offerings.

sentences.zh: 三年二月上丁，行釋菜禮，越六日，臨雍講學，自聖賢后裔，以至太學諸生，圜橋而聽者雲集。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the upper ding day of the second month, the cai libation ceremony was performed; six days later he attended the Biyong to lecture, and from descendants of sages to students of the Grand Academy, listeners gathered around the circular bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the upper ding day of the second month the cai libation was performed; six days later he lectured at the Biyong, and listeners from sage descendants to Grand Academy students crowded around the circular bridge.

sentences.zh: 七年，增聖兄孟皮從祀崇聖祠，先賢公孫僑從祀聖廟，宋臣陸秀夫、明儒曹端併入之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Sage's elder brother Meng Pi was added to secondary worship in the Chongsheng Shrine; the earlier sage Gongsun Qiao was added to secondary worship in the Sage Temple; the Song minister Lu Xiufu and the Ming Confucian Cao Duan were also included.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Meng Pi, the Sage's elder brother, was admitted to the Chongsheng Shrine; Gongsun Qiao was admitted to the Sage Temple; Song minister Lu Xiufu and Ming Confucian Cao Duan were included as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，用禮臣言，從祀盛典，以闡聖學、傳道統為斷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, following the rites officials' recommendation, for the great ceremony of secondary worship the criterion was set as expounding the Sage's learning and transmitting the lineage of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, on the rites officials' advice, the standard for secondary worship was fixed as expounding the Sage's learning and transmitting the Way's lineage.

sentences.zh: 餘各視其所行，分入忠義、名宦、鄉賢。

translations.literal: The remainder were each judged by their conduct and assigned to the categories of loyalty and righteousness, distinguished officials, and local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Others were judged by their conduct and assigned to the halls of loyalty and righteousness, distinguished officials, or local worthies.

sentences.zh: 至名臣碩輔，已配饗帝王廟者，毋再滋議。

translations.literal: As for eminent ministers and great counsellors already accorded secondary worship in the Temple of Emperors, no further proposals were to be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Eminent ministers and great counsellors already receiving secondary worship in the Temple of Emperors were not to be proposed again.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，御史劉毓楠以祔祀新章過嚴，如宋儒黃震輩均不得預，恐釀人心風俗之憂，帝責其迂謬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, censor Liu Yunan argued that the new regulations for accompanying worship were too strict—figures such as the Song Confucian Huang Zhen could not participate—and feared this would undermine public sentiment and custom; the emperor rebuked him as pedantic and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi's second year censor Liu Yunan argued that new accompanying-worship rules were too strict, excluding figures like Song Confucian Huang Zhen and risking harm to public sentiment and custom; the emperor rebuked him as pedantic.

sentences.zh: 是歲魯人毛亨，明呂棻、方孝孺並侑饗。

translations.literal: That year Mao Heng of Lu, and Lü Fen and Fang Xiaoru of Ming, were all added as secondary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mao Heng of Lu and Ming figures Lü Fen and Fang Xiaoru were all added as secondary offerings.

sentences.zh: 於是更訂增祀位次，各按時代為序。

translations.literal: Thereupon the order of positions for newly added worship was revised, each arranged by era in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The order of newly added worship positions was then revised, arranged chronologically by era.

sentences.zh: 乃定公羊高、伏勝、毛亨、孔安國、後蒼、鄭康成、范甯、陸贄、范仲淹、歐陽脩、司馬光、謝良佐、羅從彥、李綱、張栻、陸九淵、陳淳、真德秀、何基、文天祥、趙復、金履祥、陳澔、方孝孺、薛瑄、胡居仁、羅欽順、呂棻、劉宗周、孫奇逢、陸隴其列東廡，穀梁赤、高堂生、董仲舒、毛萇、杜子春、諸葛亮、王通、韓愈、胡瑗、韓琦、楊時、尹焞、胡安國、李侗、呂祖謙、黃幹、蔡沈、魏了翁、王柏、陸秀夫、許衡、吳澄、許謙、曹端、陳獻章、蔡清、王守仁、呂坤、黃道周、湯斌列西廡，並繪圖頒各省。

translations.literal: It was then fixed that Gongyang Gao, Fu Sheng, Mao Heng, Kong Anguo, Hou Cang, Zheng Xuan, Fan Ning, Lu Zhi, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, Sima Guang, Xie Liangzuo, Luo Congyan, Li Gang, Zhang Shi, Lu Jiuyuan, Chen Chun, Zhen Dexiu, He Ji, Wen Tianxiang, Zhao Fu, Jin Lüxiang, Chen Hao, Fang Xiaoru, Xue Xuan, Hu Juren, Luo Qinshun, Lü Fen, Liu Zongzhou, Sun Qifeng, and Lu Longqi were placed in the east gallery; Guliang Chi, Gaotang Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Mao Chang, Du Zichun, Zhuge Liang, Wang Tong, Han Yu, Hu Yuan, Han Qi, Yang Shi, Yin Chuo, Hu Anguo, Li Tong, Lü Zuqian, Huang Gan, Cai Shen, Wei Liaweng, Wang Bai, Lu Xiufu, Xu Heng, Wu Cheng, Xu Qian, Cao Duan, Chen Xianzhang, Cai Qing, Wang Shouren, Lü Kun, Huang Daozhou, and Tang Bin were placed in the west gallery—and portraits were issued to all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The east gallery was set for Gongyang Gao, Fu Sheng, Mao Heng, Kong Anguo, Hou Cang, Zheng Xuan, Fan Ning, Lu Zhi, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, Sima Guang, Xie Liangzuo, Luo Congyan, Li Gang, Zhang Shi, Lu Jiuyuan, Chen Chun, Zhen Dexiu, He Ji, Wen Tianxiang, Zhao Fu, Jin Lüxiang, Chen Hao, Fang Xiaoru, Xue Xuan, Hu Juren, Luo Qinshun, Lü Fen, Liu Zongzhou, Sun Qifeng, and Lu Longqi; the west for Guliang Chi, Gaotang Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Mao Chang, Du Zichun, Zhuge Liang, Wang Tong, Han Yu, Hu Yuan, Han Qi, Yang Shi, Yin Chuo, Hu Anguo, Li Tong, Lü Zuqian, Huang Gan, Cai Shen, Wei Liaweng, Wang Bai, Lu Xiufu, Xu Heng, Wu Cheng, Xu Qian, Cao Duan, Chen Xianzhang, Cai Qing, Wang Shouren, Lü Kun, Huang Daozhou, and Tang Bin—and portraits were sent to every province.

sentences.zh: 七年，以宋臣袁燮、先儒張履祥從祀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Song minister Yuan Xie and the earlier Confucian Zhang Lüxiang were admitted to secondary worship.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Song minister Yuan Xie and earlier Confucian Zhang Lüxiang were admitted to secondary worship.

sentences.zh: 光緒初元，增入先儒陸世儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, the earlier Confucian Lu Shiyi was added.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangxu earlier Confucian Lu Shiyi was added.

sentences.zh: 自是漢儒許慎、河間獻王劉德，先儒張伯行，宋儒輔廣、游酢、呂大臨並祀焉。

translations.literal: From this the Han Confucian Xu Shen, Hejian Prince Xian Liu De, the earlier Confucian Zhang Boxing, and the Song Confucians Fu Guang, You Zuo, and Lü Dalin were all worshipped together.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Han Confucian Xu Shen, Hejian Prince Xian Liu De, earlier Confucian Zhang Boxing, and Song Confucians Fu Guang, You Zuo, and Lü Dalin were all admitted to worship.

sentences.zh: 二十年仲秋上丁，親詣釋奠，仍用飲福、受胙儀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, on the upper ding day of mid-autumn, he went in person to perform the libation sacrifice, still using the ritual of drinking the blessed wine and receiving sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, on the upper ding day of mid-autumn, he performed libation in person, still observing the drinking of blessed wine and receiving of sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 三十二年冬十二月，升為大祀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the thirty-second year, it was promoted to great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirty-second year it was promoted to great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 先師祀典，自明成化、弘治間，已定八佾，十二籩、豆。

translations.literal: The sacrificial canon for the First Teacher, from the Chenghua and Hongzhi periods of Ming, had already fixed eight rows of dancers and twelve baskets and dishes.
translations.idiomatic: The First Teacher's sacrificial canon had already fixed eight rows of dancers and twelve baskets and dishes from Ming Chenghua and Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，用張璁議，始釐為中祀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, following Zhang Cong's proposal, it was first classified as medium sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing's ninth year, on Zhang Cong's proposal, it was first reduced to medium sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，祭酒王士禛嘗請酌采成、弘制，議久未行。

translations.literal: During Kangxi, libation officer Wang Shizhen once requested adopting elements from the Chenghua and Hongzhi regulations; deliberation long went unimplemented.
translations.idiomatic: During Kangxi, libation officer Wang Shizhen once asked to adopt Chenghua and Hongzhi elements; the proposal was long debated but never enacted.

sentences.zh: 至是命禮臣具儀上，奏言：「孔子德參兩大，道冠百王。

translations.literal: At this point the rites officials were ordered to submit ritual specifications, stating: "Confucius's virtue matched Heaven and Earth; his Way surpassed all kings.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials were then ordered to submit ritual specifications, stating: "Confucius's virtue matched Heaven and Earth; his Way surpassed all kings.

sentences.zh: 自漢至明，典多缺略。

translations.literal: From Han through Ming, the canon was largely incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Ming the canon had been largely incomplete.

sentences.zh: 我聖祖釋奠闕里，三跪九拜，曲柄黃蓋，留供廟庭。

translations.literal: Our sage ancestor performed libation at Qufu with three kneelings and nine prostrations; the curved-handle yellow canopy was left as an offering in the temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage ancestor sacrificed at Qufu with three kneelings and nine prostrations and left the curved-handle yellow canopy in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨雍，止稱詣學。

translations.literal: When Shizong attended the Biyong, it was simply termed going to the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong attended the Biyong, the rite was simply called going to the academy.

sentences.zh: 案前上香、奠帛、獻爵，跪而不立。

translations.literal: Before the altar he offered incense, silk, and libation cups—all kneeling, never standing.
translations.idiomatic: At the altar he offered incense, silk, and cups—all while kneeling, never standing.

sentences.zh: 黃瓦飾廟，五代封王。

translations.literal: Yellow tiles adorned the temple; in the Five Dynasties he was enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow tiles adorned the temple, and in the Five Dynasties he was enfeoffed as king.

sentences.zh: 聖誕致齋，聖諱敬避。

translations.literal: On the Sage's birthday there was fasting; the Sage's taboo name was reverently avoided.
translations.idiomatic: On the Sage's birthday fasting was observed and his taboo name reverently avoided.

sentences.zh: 高宗釋奠，均法聖祖，躬行三獻，垂為常儀。

translations.literal: When Gaozong performed libation, he followed the sage ancestor in all respects, personally conducting three offerings—established as constant ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's libation followed the sage ancestor in all respects, with three offerings performed in person—established as standard ritual.

sentences.zh: 崇德報功，遠軼前代。

translations.literal: Honoring virtue and rewarding merit, it far surpassed previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In honoring virtue and rewarding merit, it far surpassed earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 已隱寓升大祀至意。

translations.literal: This already implicitly conveyed the intent to promote it to great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: This already implicitly expressed the intent to promote it to great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 世宗諭言：『堯舜禹湯文武之道，賴孔子以不墜。

translations.literal: Shizong's instruction stated: 'The Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wen and Wu depended on Confucius not to fall away.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong instructed: 'The Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wen and Wu depended on Confucius to endure.

sentences.zh: 魯論一書，尤切日用，能使萬世倫紀明，名分辨，人心正，風俗端，此所以為生民未有也。』

translations.literal: The Analects of Lu is especially practical for daily life; it can clarify the moral order for ten thousand generations, distinguish names and roles, rectify hearts and minds, and set customs upright—this is why he had never existed among the people.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects is especially practical for daily life; it clarifies moral order for all ages, distinguishes names and roles, rectifies hearts, and sets customs upright—this is why he was unmatched among the people.'

sentences.zh: 聖訓煌煌，後先一揆。

translations.literal: The sage instruction shone brilliantly; earlier and later were of one measure.
translations.idiomatic: The sage instruction shone brilliantly; earlier and later rulers were of one mind.

sentences.zh: 近雖學派紛歧，而顯示欽崇，自足收經正民興巨效。」

translations.literal: Though in recent times scholarly schools have diverged, clearly displaying reverence and esteem is sufficient to achieve the great effect of rectifying the classics and rousing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though scholarly schools have diverged in recent times, clearly displaying reverence is enough to achieve the great effect of rectifying the classics and rousing the people.

sentences.zh: 疏上，於是文廟改覆黃瓦，樂用八佾，增武舞，釋奠躬詣，有事遣親王代，分獻四配用大學士，十二哲兩廡用尚書。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Confucian temple was re-roofed with yellow tiles; music used eight rows; martial dance was added; the emperor went in person for libation, or when occupied sent a prince; the four associates were distributed to by grand secretaries; the twelve wise ones and two galleries by board presidents.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, the Confucian temple was re-roofed with yellow tiles; music used eight rows and martial dance was added; the emperor went in person for libation or sent a prince when occupied; grand secretaries distributed to the four associates and board presidents to the twelve wise ones and two galleries.

sentences.zh: 祀日入大成左門，升階入殿左門，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day he entered through the left Gate of Great Completion, ascended the steps and entered through the left hall gate, performing three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day he entered by the left Gate of Great Completion, ascended the steps through the left hall gate, and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 上香，奠帛、爵俱跪。

translations.literal: Offering incense, silk, and libation cups—all kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: Incense, silk, and libation cups were all offered kneeling.

sentences.zh: 三獻俱親行。

translations.literal: All three offerings were performed in person.
translations.idiomatic: He personally performed all three offerings.

sentences.zh: 出亦如之。

translations.literal: Departure was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Departure followed the same form.

sentences.zh: 遣代則四配用尚書，餘用侍郎，出入自右門，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: When a substitute was dispatched, board presidents handled the four associates and vice presidents the rest; entry and exit were through the right gate, without drinking blessed wine or receiving sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: When a substitute was sent, board presidents handled the four associates and vice presidents the rest; he entered and exited by the right gate and did not drink blessed wine or receive sacrificial meat.

sentences.zh: 崇聖祠本改親王承祭，若代釋奠，則以大學士為之。

translations.literal: The Chongsheng Shrine was originally changed so a prince would preside; if substituting for libation, a grand secretary would do so.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongsheng Shrine was changed so a prince would preside; if substituting for libation, a grand secretary would perform it.

sentences.zh: 分獻配位用侍郎，西廡用內閣學士。

translations.literal: Distribution for associate positions used vice presidents; the west gallery used grand secretaries of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice presidents distributed to associate positions; grand secretaries of the Secretariat distributed to the west gallery.

sentences.zh: 餘如故。

translations.literal: The remainder was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else remained as before.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，定文廟九楹三階五陛制。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, the Confucian temple was fixed at nine bays, three steps, and five terraces.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year the Confucian temple was fixed at nine bays, three steps, and five terraces.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啟霖請以王夫之、黃宗羲、顧炎武從祀。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin requested that Wang Fuzhi, Huang Zongxi, and Gu Yanwu be admitted to secondary worship.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Qilin requested secondary worship for Wang Fuzhi, Huang Zongxi, and Gu Yanwu.

sentences.zh: 下部議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the boards for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the boards for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 先是署禮部侍郎郭嵩燾、湖北學政孔祥霖請夫之從祀，江西學政陳寶琛請宗羲、炎武從祀，並被駁。

translations.literal: Previously acting vice president of Rites Guo Songtao and Hubei educational commissioner Kong Xianglin had requested Fuzhi; Jiangxi educational commissioner Chen Baochen had requested Zongxi and Yanwu—all were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Previously acting Rites vice president Guo Songtao and Hubei commissioner Kong Xianglin had requested Fuzhi; Jiangxi commissioner Chen Baochen had requested Zongxi and Yanwu—all had been rejected.

sentences.zh: 至是部議謂：「三人生當明季，毅然以窮經為天下倡，德性問學，尊道並行，第夫之黃書，原極諸篇，託旨春秋；

translations.literal: Now the board stated: "The three lived in late Ming, resolutely taking exhaustive study of the classics as their banner for the realm; moral nature and inquiry into learning, reverence for the Way—all practiced together. However, in Fuzhi's Yellow Book and essays such as 'Tracing the Origins,' the intent is carried in the Spring and Autumn;
translations.idiomatic: Now the board stated: "All three lived in late Ming and resolutely championed exhaustive study of the classics; moral nature, inquiry, and reverence for the Way went together. Yet in Fuzhi's Yellow Book and 'Tracing the Origins' essays the intent is carried in the Spring and Autumn;

sentences.zh: 宗羲明夷待訪錄，原君、原臣諸篇，取義孟子，似近偏激。

translations.literal: Zongxi's Waiting for Visitors in the Mingyi and essays such as 'On the Ruler' and 'On the Minister' take their meaning from Mencius and seem somewhat radical.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxi's Waiting for Visitors in the Mingyi and essays like 'On the Ruler' and 'On the Minister' draw on Mencius and seem somewhat radical.

sentences.zh: 惟炎武醇乎其醇，應允炎武從祀，夫之、宗羲候裁定。」

translations.literal: Only Yanwu is purest of the pure; Yanwu's secondary worship should be approved; Fuzhi and Zongxi await final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanwu is purest of the pure; Yanwu's secondary worship should be approved, while Fuzhi and Zongxi await final decision.

sentences.zh: 帝命並祀之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered all three worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all three admitted to worship.

sentences.zh: 闕里文廟，有事祭告，具前祭告篇。

translations.literal: At the Qufu Confucian temple, when there was occasion for sacrificial announcement, the previous announcement text was used.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qufu Confucian temple, sacrificial announcements used the established announcement text.

sentences.zh: 春、秋致祭同太學。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn sacrifices were the same as at the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn sacrifices followed the Grand Academy form.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，聖祖東巡親祭，禮部具儀。

translations.literal: During Kangxi, the sage ancestor on his eastern tour sacrificed in person; the Board of Rites provided the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: During Kangxi the sage ancestor sacrificed in person on his eastern tour; the Board of Rites supplied the ritual.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕次日，帝服龍袞，行在儀仗具陳，行禮二跪六拜，配位、十哲、兩廡、啟聖祠，皆遣官分獻。

translations.literal: The day after the imperial halt, the emperor wore dragon robes; travel regalia was fully displayed; the rite was two kneelings and six bows; associate positions, ten wise ones, two galleries, and Qisheng Shrine—all had officials dispatched for distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The day after the imperial halt the emperor wore dragon robes with full travel regalia and performed two kneelings and six bows; officials were dispatched to distribute offerings at the associate positions, ten wise ones, two galleries, and Qisheng Shrine.

sentences.zh: 扈從諸臣，文官知府、武官副將以上，衍聖公暨各氏子孫在職者，咸陪祀。

translations.literal: Accompanying officials—civil officials of prefect rank and above, military officials of vice commander and above, the Duke for the Propagation of Sagehood and employed descendants of the clans—all attended sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying officials—prefects and above, vice commanders and above, the Duke for the Propagation of Sagehood, and employed clan descendants—all attended the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 聖心猶未安，命更議。

translations.literal: The sage heart was still uneasy; he ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Still unsatisfied, the emperor ordered further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尋定迎神、送神俱三跪九拜，惟樂章與國學小異，可令太常司樂及樂舞生先往肄習。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that receiving and sending the spirit both used three kneelings and nine prostrations; only the music differed slightly from the National Academy—musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and dance students could be sent ahead to practice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon receiving and sending the spirit were both fixed at three kneelings and nine prostrations; only the music differed slightly from the National Academy, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians and dance students could be sent ahead to practice.

sentences.zh: 帝親制祝文。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed the prayer text.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself composed the prayer text.

sentences.zh: 祀日詣廟，至奎文閣前降輦，如齋所小憩，自大次出，入大成門，登殿釋奠畢，御詩禮堂講書。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day he went to the temple, descended from the carriage before Kuiwen Pavilion, rested briefly as at the fasting lodge, emerged from the great tent, entered the Gate of Great Completion, ascended the hall for libation; then lectured on classics in the Hall of Ritual with an imperial poem.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day he went to the temple, descended before Kuiwen Pavilion, rested briefly as at the fasting lodge, emerged from the great tent, entered the Gate of Great Completion, ascended for libation, then lectured in the Hall of Ritual and composed an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 禮成，周視廟庭車服、禮器。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he toured the temple courtyard's chariots, robes, and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete he toured the temple courtyard's chariots, robes, and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 更常服，駕如孔林，跪奠酒，三爵，三拜，賜衍聖公以下銀幣有差。

translations.literal: Changing to ordinary dress, he drove to the Kong forest, knelt to pour wine—three cups, three bows—and granted silver coins to the Duke for Propagation of Sagehood and below in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Changing to ordinary dress, he drove to the Kong forest, knelt to pour three cups of wine and bow three times, and granted silver coins in graded amounts to the Duke for Propagation of Sagehood and those below.

sentences.zh: 留曲柄黃蓋陳廟庭。

translations.literal: The curved-handle yellow canopy was left displayed in the temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The curved-handle yellow canopy was left on display in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 擴孔林地畝，蠲其稅。

translations.literal: The acreage of the Kong forest was expanded and its tax remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Kong forest's acreage was expanded and its tax remitted.

sentences.zh: 建廟碑，御書文鑱石。

translations.literal: A temple stele was erected; the imperial text was carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: A temple stele was erected with the imperial text carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 又建子思子廟，仿顏、曾、孟三廟制。

translations.literal: Also a temple to Zisi was built, modeled on the three temples of Yan, Zeng, and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: A temple to Zisi was also built, modeled on the three temples of Yan, Zeng, and Meng.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，修文廟成，皇子往祭，行禮杏壇。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, when renovation of the Confucian temple was complete, a prince was sent to sacrifice; the rite was performed at the Apricot Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, when the Confucian temple renovation was complete, a prince was sent to sacrifice at the Apricot Altar.

sentences.zh: ，曲阜廟災，遣官詣闕里祭慰，敕大臣重建，並令闕里司樂遣人赴太常習樂舞，冠服悉准太學式為之。

translations.literal: The Qufu temple suffered fire; officials were dispatched to Qufu for sacrificial condolence; ministers were ordered to rebuild; Qufu musicians were sent to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to learn music and dance; caps and robes were all made to Grand Academy standards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qufu temple burned, officials were sent for sacrificial condolence, ministers were ordered to rebuild, Qufu musicians were sent to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to learn music and dance, and caps and robes were made to Grand Academy standards.

sentences.zh: 八年，廟成，黃瓦畫棟，悉仿宮殿制。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the temple was complete, yellow tiles and painted rafters all followed palace standards.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was completed in the eighth year, yellow tiles and painted rafters all matched palace standards.

sentences.zh: 凡登、簋、簠、鉶、籩、豆、尊、爵，頒自上方。

translations.literal: All ding tripods, gui vessels, fu containers, meat stands, baskets, dishes, wine jars, and libation cups were issued from the court.
translations.idiomatic: All ding, gui, fu, meat stands, baskets, dishes, wine jars, and libation cups were issued from the court.

sentences.zh: 勒碑如故事。

translations.literal: A stele was inscribed as per precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A stele was inscribed as usual.

sentences.zh: 特詔皇五子往祭。

translations.literal: A special edict ordered the fifth imperial son to go and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict ordered the fifth imperial son to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 至各省府、州、縣釋奠，以所在印官承祭，禮如太學，順治初行之。

translations.literal: As for libation sacrifice in provinces, prefectures, districts, and counties, the local seal-holding official presided; the rite was as at the Grand Academy—implemented from early Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial, prefectural, district, and county libation was presided over by the local seal-holding official, following the Grand Academy form from early Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，定制各省督、撫、學政上丁率屬致祭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, it was fixed that governors-general, governors, and educational commissioners in each province on upper ding day would lead their subordinates in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng's fifth year it was fixed that on upper ding day each province's governor-general, governor, and educational commissioner would lead subordinates in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 學政蒞試時，先至文廟行禮，府、州、縣官率屬於治所文廟行。

translations.literal: When educational commissioners arrived for examinations, they first went to the Confucian temple to perform the rite; prefectural, district, and county officials led subordinates at the local Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: When educational commissioners arrived for examinations they first sacrificed at the Confucian temple; prefectural, district, and county officials led subordinates at their local temples.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，敕直省學宮設先賢、先儒神位。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong, an edict ordered provincial academies to set up spirit tablets for earlier sages and earlier Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's sixth year an edict ordered provincial academies to install spirit tablets for earlier sages and Confucians.

sentences.zh: 同治初，頒從祀先儒位次圖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, charts of the order of earlier Confucians in secondary worship were issued.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tongzhi charts showing the order of earlier Confucians in secondary worship were issued.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，升大祀，各省文廟規制、禮器、樂舞暨崇聖祠祭品，並視太學，禮節悉從舊。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangxu, when it was promoted to great sacrifice, the standards, ritual vessels, music and dance of provincial Confucian temples and the offerings of the Chongsheng Shrine all followed the Grand Academy; ceremonial details all followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Guangxu, after promotion to great sacrifice, provincial Confucian temples' standards, vessels, music, and dance and the Chongsheng Shrine offerings all matched the Grand Academy; ceremonial details followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 元聖周公，給事中黏本盛奏請文廟後別立傳聖祠。

translations.literal: The Original Sage Duke of Zhou—Supervising Secretary Nian Bensheng memorialized requesting a separate Chuan Sheng Shrine behind the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the Original Sage Duke of Zhou, Supervising Secretary Nian Bensheng memorialized to establish a separate Chuan Sheng Shrine behind the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 下部議，禮臣言：「祭祀周公，向在太學。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the boards; rites officials stated: "Sacrifice to the Duke of Zhou had formerly been at the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the boards; rites officials stated: "Sacrifice to the Duke of Zhou had formerly been at the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 至唐顯慶間，以公制禮作樂，功侔帝王，就饗儒宮，欲尊反貶。

translations.literal: By the Xianqing period of Tang, because the Duke established rites and made music and his achievement matched emperors, he was given feast at the Confucian academy—intending to honor but actually demeaning.
translations.idiomatic: By Tang Xianqing, because the Duke established rites and made music and his achievement matched emperors, he was feasted at the Confucian academy—intending honor but actually demeaning him.

sentences.zh: 始定配饗帝王廟，既不與孔子並祭太學，乃反立傳聖祠於其後，殊失尊崇本意也。」

translations.literal: It was then fixed that he received secondary worship in the Temple of Emperors; since he no longer received joint sacrifice with Confucius at the Grand Academy, yet a Chuan Sheng Shrine was erected behind it—this greatly lost the original intent of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given secondary worship in the Temple of Emperors; no longer sacrificed with Confucius at the Grand Academy, yet a Chuan Sheng Shrine was placed behind it—greatly contrary to the intent of reverence.

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，聖祖祀闕里，詔言：「周公古大聖人，制禮作樂，垂法萬世，廟在曲阜，應行致祭。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, when the sage ancestor sacrificed at Qufu, an edict stated: "The Duke of Zhou was an ancient great sage; he established rites and made music, leaving standards for ten thousand generations; his temple is at Qufu and sacrifice should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's twenty-third year, when the sage ancestor sacrificed at Qufu, an edict stated: "The Duke of Zhou was an ancient great sage who established rites and made music, leaving standards for all ages; his temple at Qufu should receive sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乃遣親王及禮部尚書往焉。

translations.literal: A prince and the president of the Board of Rites were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: A prince and the Board of Rites president were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 親制祝文。

translations.literal: He personally composed the prayer text.
translations.idiomatic: He himself composed the prayer text.

sentences.zh: 祭禮，三獻。

translations.literal: The sacrificial rite: three offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice used three offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭品：羊一、豕一、果五盤、尊一、爵三，敕有司治辦。

translations.literal: Offerings: one sheep, one pig, five plates of fruit, one wine jar, three libation cups—local officials were ordered to prepare them.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were one sheep, one pig, five plates of fruit, one wine jar, and three libation cups—local officials were ordered to prepare them.

sentences.zh: 明年，授東野氏一人博士，奉祀祠廟。

translations.literal: The next year one person of the Dongye clan was appointed erudite to tend the shrine and temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next year one member of the Dongye clan was appointed erudite to tend the shrine and temple.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，御書周公廟碑文，依文廟式，勒之貞珉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the imperial text for the Duke of Zhou temple stele, following Confucian temple precedent, was carved in enduring stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the imperial Duke of Zhou temple stele text, following Confucian temple precedent, was carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，東巡，增登一，鉶二，簋、簠各二，籩、豆各八，遣親王一人行禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong, on the eastern tour, one ding was added, two meat stands, two gui and two fu each, eight baskets and eight dishes each; one prince was dispatched to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's twelfth year, on the eastern tour, offerings were increased by one ding, two meat stands, two gui and two fu, and eight baskets and eight dishes each; one prince was dispatched to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 其祀配饗魯公，遣禮部尚書行。

translations.literal: At that sacrifice the Duke of Lu received secondary worship; the president of the Board of Rites was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: At that sacrifice the Duke of Lu received secondary worship, performed by the dispatched Board of Rites president.

sentences.zh: 明年，幸曲阜，親詣上香，一跪三拜。

translations.literal: The next year, visiting Qufu, he went in person to offer incense—one kneeling and three bows.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, visiting Qufu, he offered incense in person with one kneeling and three bows.

sentences.zh: 自是東巡親詣以為常。

translations.literal: From this, personal attendance on eastern tours became customary.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter personal attendance on eastern tours became customary.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，依孔氏南宗例，置當陽博士，奉祀陵墓。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, following the precedent of the southern branch of the Kong clan, a Dangyang erudite was appointed to tend the tomb and shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, following the southern Kong clan precedent, a Dangyang erudite was appointed to tend the tomb and shrine.

sentences.zh: 關聖帝君清初都盛京，建廟地載門外，賜額「義高千古」。

translations.literal: Lord Guan the Sage Emperor—in early Qing at the capital in Shenjing, a temple was built outside Dizai Gate, granted the plaque "Righteousness High Through the Ages."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Guan the Sage Emperor—in early Qing at the Shenjing capital a temple was built outside Dizai Gate and granted the plaque "Righteousness High Through the Ages."

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，復建廟地安門外，歲以五月十三日致祭。

translations.literal: When Shizu entered the pass, a temple was rebuilt outside Di'an Gate; sacrifice was performed annually on the thirteenth day of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu entered the pass a temple was rebuilt outside Di'an Gate, with annual sacrifice on the thirteenth day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，敕封忠義神武關聖大帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, by imperial edict he was enfeoffed as the Loyal and Righteous, Divine and Martial Lord Guan the Great Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, by imperial edict he was enfeoffed as the Loyal and Righteous, Divine and Martial Lord Guan the Great Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，追封三代公爵，曾祖曰光昭，祖曰裕昌，父曰成忠，供後殿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, three generations were posthumously enfeoffed as dukes—the great-grandfather titled Guangzhao, the grandfather Yuchang, the father Chengzhong—and enshrined in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3, three ancestors were posthumously raised to ducal rank—Great-grandfather Guangzhao, Grandfather Yuchang, Father Chengzhong—and installed in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 增春、秋二祭。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn sacrifices were added.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn sacrifices were added.

sentences.zh: 洛陽、解州後裔並授五經博士，世襲承祀。

translations.literal: Descendants of Luoyang and Jiezhou were both appointed Erudites of the Five Classics, hereditarily to continue the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants from both Luoyang and Jiezhou were appointed Erudites of the Five Classics, inheriting the duty of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尋定春、秋祀儀，前殿大臣承祭，後殿以太常長官。

translations.literal: Soon the spring and autumn sacrificial rites were fixed: in the front hall a minister performed the sacrifice; in the rear hall the chief officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The spring and autumn rites were soon fixed: a minister sacrificed in the front hall, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' chief officer in the rear.

sentences.zh: 屆日質明，大臣朝服入廟左門，升階就拜位，上香，行三跪九拜禮。

translations.literal: On the appointed day at dawn, the minister in court dress entered the temple's left gate, ascended the steps to the kneeling position, offered incense, and performed the rite of three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the appointed day the minister entered in court dress by the temple's left gate, ascended to his place, offered incense, and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 三獻，不飲福、受胙。

translations.literal: Three offerings; he did not drink the blessed wine or receive the sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings were made; the blessed wine was not drunk and the sacrificial meat not received.

sentences.zh: 祭後殿二跪六拜。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the rear hall: two kneelings and six prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The rear hall received two kneelings and six prostrations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，增當陽博士一人奉冢祀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, one more Erudite from Dangyang was added to maintain tomb sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year an Erudite from Dangyang was added to maintain the tomb sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 直省關帝廟亦一歲三祭，用太牢。

translations.literal: In the direct provinces, Guandi temples also held three sacrifices a year, using the tai lao offering.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Guandi temples likewise held three sacrifices yearly, with the grand tai lao offering.

sentences.zh: 先期承祭官致齋，不理刑名，前殿印官，後殿丞、史，陳設禮儀，略如京師。

translations.literal: Beforehand the officiating officer observed the fast and did not attend to criminal cases; for the front hall, the principal officer; for the rear hall, the assistant and recorder; the arrangement of ritual was roughly as in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The officiating officer fasted beforehand and set aside criminal business; the principal officer served the front hall, the assistant and recorder the rear—arrangements broadly matching the capital.

sentences.zh: 文昌帝君明成化間，因元祠重建。

translations.literal: Lord Wenchang: in the Ming Chenghua period, rebuilt on the site of the Yuan temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord Wenchang temple was rebuilt in the Ming Chenghua reign on the site of the old Yuan shrine.

sentences.zh: 在京師地安門外，久圮。

translations.literal: It stood outside Di'an Gate in the capital and had long fallen into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Di'an Gate in the capital, it had long lain in ruins.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，潼江寇平，初寇闚梓潼，望見祠山旗幟，卻退。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, when the Tongjiang bandits were pacified—initially the bandits had looked toward Zitong, saw banners on the temple mountain, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5, after the Tongjiang rebels were suppressed: they had earlier approached Zitong, seen the temple banners on the mountain, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 至是御書「化成耆定」額，用彰異績。

translations.literal: At this the emperor personally wrote the plaque "Transformation Complete, Long Peace Established" to manifest the extraordinary achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wrote in his own hand the plaque "Transformation Complete, Long Peace Established" to honor the extraordinary feat.

sentences.zh: 發中帑重新祠宇，明年夏告成，仁宗躬謁九拜，詔稱：「帝君主持文運，崇聖辟邪，海內尊奉，與關聖同，允宜列入祀典。」

translations.literal: Funds from the central treasury were issued to rebuild the temple; the next summer it was completed; Renzong personally visited and made nine prostrations; the edict stated: "The Lord presides over the literary fortune, venerates sages and wards off evil; honored throughout the realm like Lord Guan—it is fitting to enter the register of sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Central funds rebuilt the shrine; it was finished the following summer. Renzong paid a personal visit and prostrated nine times. The edict read: "The Lord presides over literary fortune, exalts the sages and repels evil; the realm honors him as it does Lord Guan—he should enter the state sacrificial canon."

sentences.zh: 於是大學士硃珪撰碑記，略言：「文昌星載天官書，所謂『斗魁六星，戴匡曰文昌宮』是也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Secretary Zhu Gui composed a stele inscription, stating in summary: "The Wenchang star is recorded in the Book of the Celestial Offices—what is called 'the six stars of the Dipper's head, the girdle called the Wenchang Palace' is this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui then wrote the stele, noting in brief: "The Wenchang star appears in the Book of the Celestial Offices—the 'six stars of the Dipper's head, the girdle called the Wenchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 尚書『禋六宗』，孔疏引鄭玄云：『皆天神，司中、司命，文昌第五、第四星也。』

translations.literal: In the Book of Documents, 'sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones'—Kong Yingda's commentary cites Zheng Xuan: 'All are celestial deities—Sizhong and Siming are the fifth and fourth stars of Wenchang.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents' 'sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones'—Kong Yingda, citing Zheng Xuan: 'They are celestial powers; Sizhong and Siming are Wenchang's fifth and fourth stars.'

sentences.zh: 周禮大宗伯：『以燎祀司中、司命。』

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Minister of Rites: 'Sacrifice by burnt offering to Sizhong and Siming.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Grand Minister of Rites: 'By burnt offering sacrifice to Sizhong and Siming.'

sentences.zh: 鄭注謂文昌星。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary identifies them as the Wenchang star.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan identifies these as the Wenchang star.

sentences.zh: 然則文昌之祀，始有虞，著周禮，漢、晉且配郊祀。

translations.literal: Thus sacrifice to Wenchang began under Yu of the Shun, was set forth in the Rites of Zhou, and in Han and Jin was even included in suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang worship thus began under Emperor Yu, was codified in the Rites of Zhou, and in Han and Jin shared in suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 元命苞云：『上將建威武，次將正左右，貴相理文緒，司祿賞功進士。』

translations.literal: The Yuanming bao says: 'The Senior General establishes martial might, the Junior General rectifies left and right, the Noble Minister governs literary threads, Silu rewards merit and advances scholars.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanming bao states: 'The Senior General establishes martial prowess, the Junior General sets left and right aright, the Noble Minister orders the threads of culture, Silu bestows rank and advances successful candidates.'

sentences.zh: 是爵祿、科舉職司久矣。

translations.literal: Thus the charge over ranks, emoluments, and the civil examinations is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: So jurisdiction over rank, salary, and the examination halls is ancient.

sentences.zh: 又言帝君周初為張仲，孝友顯化，隋、唐為王通，徵李商隱張亞子廟詩，讀孫樵祭梓潼神君文，化書：唐開元命為左丞，通考：僖宗封為濟順王，宋真宗改號英顯，哲宗加封輔元開化文昌司祿帝君，元加號宏仁，蓋可考見雲。」

translations.literal: Again it states that the Lord in early Zhou was Zhang Zhong, manifesting filial brotherhood; in Sui and Tang he was Wang Tong; citing Li Shangyin's poem to the Zhang Yazi temple, reading Sun Qiao's essay sacrificing to the Zitong spirit lord; Huashu: in Tang Kaiyuan appointed Left Vice Director; Tongkao: Emperor Xizong enfeoffed him as Prince Jishun; Song Zhenzong changed the title to Yingxian; Zhezong added the title Assistant Originator, Opener of Culture, Wenchang Silu Lord; the Yuan added Hongren—all of which can be verified."
translations.idiomatic: The inscription also traced the Lord through history—as Zhang Zhong in early Zhou, famed for filial piety; as Wang Tong in Sui and Tang; citing Li Shangyin's hymn to the Zhang Yazi shrine and Sun Qiao's prayer to the Zitong spirit; Huashu records Tang Xuanzong's appointment as Left Vice Director; the Comprehensive Exam notes Xizong's enfeoffment as Prince Jishun; Zhenzong's title Yingxian; Zhezong's elevation to Assistant Originator, Opener of Culture, Wenchang Silu Lord; and the Yuan addition of Hongren—each attested in the sources."

sentences.zh: 禮官遂定議。

translations.literal: The ritual officers then finalized the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites then settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 歲春祭以二月初三誕日，秋祭，仲秋諏吉將事，遣大臣往。

translations.literal: Each year the spring sacrifice fell on the second month's third day, his birthday; the autumn sacrifice, at mid-autumn an auspicious day was chosen and the rite dispatched, with a minister sent.
translations.idiomatic: Spring sacrifice each year on the second month's third day, his birth date; autumn sacrifice at mid-autumn on a chosen auspicious day, with a minister dispatched.

sentences.zh: 前殿供正神，後殿則祀其先世，祀典如關帝。

translations.literal: The front hall enshrined the principal deity; the rear hall worshipped his ancestors; the sacrificial canon was as for Lord Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The front hall held the principal deity, the rear his forebears—the canon matching Lord Guan's.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，躋中祀，禮臣請崇殿階，拓規制，遣王承祭，後殿以太常長官親詣，二跪六拜，樂六奏，文舞八佾，允行。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, promoted to mid-level sacrifice; ritual officers requested elevated hall steps and expanded scale; a prince to perform sacrifice; the rear hall visited in person by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chief, two kneelings six prostrations, six musical performances, civil dance in eight rows—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6 worship was raised to mid-tier rite. Ritual officers asked for loftier steps and enlarged precincts; a prince was to sacrifice, the rear hall to receive the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chief in person—two kneelings, six prostrations, six stanzas of music, eight rows of civil dancers. All was approved.

sentences.zh: 直省文昌廟有司以時饗祀，無祠廟者，設位公所祭之。

translations.literal: In the direct provinces, Wenchang temples were feasted on schedule by local officers; where no temple existed, a place was set up in the public hall for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Wenchang shrines received timely offerings from local officers; where no temple stood, a seat was set in the yamen hall.

sentences.zh: 畢，徹位隨祝帛送燎。

translations.literal: When complete, the positions were withdrawn and, with the prayer silks, sent to the burnt offering.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the tablets were removed and the prayer silks committed to the flame.

sentences.zh: 旗纛之祭天命十年，定瀋陽，還軍扈渾河，刲牛祭纛。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to battle standards: in the tenth year of Tianming, settling Shenyang, the army returned escorting the Hun River, slaughtered an ox and sacrificed to the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the battle standard began in Tianming 10: after settling Shenyang the army returned along the Hun River and sacrificed an ox before the standard.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年征朝鮮，明年凱旋，並立纛拜天。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong campaigning against Korea, the next year on triumphant return, both erected the standard and worshipped Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1, on the Korea campaign, they returned victorious the next year, erecting the standard and bowing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自是出征班師祭纛以為常，時旗纛附祀關帝廟也。

translations.literal: From then on, sacrifice to the standard on departure and return became customary; at the time the standard was also attached to worship at Lord Guan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter offering to the standard at departure and return became fixed practice; for a time the standard shared Lord Guan's temple.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關後，始行望祭。

translations.literal: After Shizu entered the pass, distant-worship sacrifice was first performed.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Shizu entered the pass did the court perform the distant standard rite.

sentences.zh: 凡親征諏吉啟行，先於堂子內門外建御營黃龍大纛，按翼分設八旗大纛、火器營大纛各八，列其後，並北鄉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor personally campaigned, on the chosen auspicious day of departure, first outside the inner gate of the Tangzi the imperial camp's yellow dragon great standard was erected; flanking wings set eight great standards of each banner and eight of the firearms camp, arrayed behind, all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: On a personally led campaign, after the auspicious day was chosen, outside the Tangzi inner gate they raised the imperial yellow dragon standard, with eight banner standards and eight firearms-camp standards on each flank, all facing north behind it.

sentences.zh: 帝御戎服佩刀，出宮乘騎，入堂子街門降。

translations.literal: The emperor in martial dress wearing his sword, left the palace mounted, entered Tangzi Street Gate and dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the palace in martial dress, sword at side, mounted; at the Tangzi street gate he dismounted.

sentences.zh: 圜殿禮畢，出內門致禮纛神，率從征將士三跪九拜，不贊。

translations.literal: When the round hall rite was complete, exiting the inner gate he performed obeisance to the standard spirit; leading the campaign generals and soldiers in three kneelings and nine prostrations, without a ceremonial intoner.
translations.idiomatic: After rites in the round hall, he passed the inner gate to honor the standard spirit, leading the host in three kneelings and nine prostrations—without a liturgist.

sentences.zh: 禮成樂作，鑾駕啟行，領侍衛內大臣、司纛侍衛率親軍舉纛從。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete music sounded; the imperial carriage set out; the leading Bodyguard grand minister and standard-bearing guards led the personal troops raising the standard in escort.
translations.idiomatic: Music sounded; the imperial train moved out—the chief Bodyguard minister and standard-bearers leading the household troops with the raised standard.

sentences.zh: 凱旋致祭，屆日陳法駕鹵簿，自郊外五里訖堂子門外。

translations.literal: On triumphant return and offering sacrifice, on the appointed day the statutory imperial guard of honor was arrayed from five li outside the city to outside the Tangzi gate.
translations.idiomatic: On victorious return, the statutory guard of honor was drawn up from five li beyond the walls to the Tangzi gate.

sentences.zh: 駕至郊，降輿拜纛如儀。

translations.literal: When the carriage reached the suburbs, he descended and bowed to the standard according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburbs he left the carriage and bowed to the standard as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 命將出師亦如之。

translations.literal: When generals were ordered to take the field, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same rite attended a general's departure.

sentences.zh: 聖祖征噶爾丹凱旋，翼日為壇安定門外，致祭隨營旗纛，用太牢，始遣大臣行禮。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor returned victorious from campaigning against Galdan, the next day an altar was raised outside Anding Gate; sacrifice was performed to the campaign standards, using tai lao; for the first time a minister was dispatched to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: After Kangxi's victory over Galdan, an altar was raised outside Anding Gate the next day; the campaign standards received tai lao sacrifice, and for the first time a minister performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，定三年一祭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, it was fixed at one sacrifice every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng the interval was set at once every three years.

sentences.zh: 凡旗纛皆庋內府，祭則設之。

translations.literal: All standards were stored in the Inner Palace Storehouse and set out for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: All standards were kept in the imperial storehouse and brought out only for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 各省祭旗纛，則遣武官戎服行禮焉。

translations.literal: In the provinces, sacrifice to the standards was performed by a military officer in martial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Provincially, armored military officers performed the standard rite.

sentences.zh: 砲位之祭，，造紅衣砲，鐫曰天佑助威大將軍，遂攜以毀於子章台，克大凌河，行軍攜紅衣砲始此。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to cannon positions: red-coated cannon were cast, inscribed "Heaven's Aid, Aiding Might, Great General," then carried to destroy Zizhang Platform; taking Great Ling River, carrying red-coated cannon on campaign began here.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon sacrifice originated when red-coated guns were cast inscribed "Heaven's Aid, Aiding Might, Great General," borne to batter Zizhang Platform; from the taking of Dalin River, field armies began carrying red-coated cannon.

sentences.zh: 厥後敕漢軍齎砲進關。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Han Army was ordered to carry cannon through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han Banner troops were then ordered to bring cannon through the pass.

sentences.zh: 世祖奠鼎燕京，定制以歲季秋朔，陳砲位盧溝橋沙鍋村，席地為壇，西鄉，以八旗漢軍都統將事。

translations.literal: When Shizu established the capital at Yanjing, the rule was fixed: each year's first day of late autumn, cannon positions displayed at Shaguo Village by Lugou Bridge; an altar on the ground, facing west; the Eight Banners Han Army commanders-in-chief presiding.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shizu fixed the capital at Yanjing, each late-autumn new moon cannon were arrayed at Shaguo Village by the Lugou Bridge—an earthen altar facing west, presided over by the Han Banner commanders.

sentences.zh: 分旗翼列，用果品、少牢。

translations.literal: Arranged in banner wings; fruit and xiao lao offerings used.
translations.idiomatic: Banner wings were deployed; offerings were fruit and xiao lao.

sentences.zh: 屆時先鑲黃旗砲位，都統御補服，上香，三跪九拜，三獻，讀祝。

translations.literal: At the appointed time, first the Bordered Yellow Banner cannon position; the commander in surcoat offered incense, three kneelings nine prostrations, three offerings, reading the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, the Bordered Yellow Banner cannon came first; its commander in formal surcoat offered incense, three kneelings and nine prostrations, three offerings, and read the prayer.

sentences.zh: 餘七砲位亦如之。

translations.literal: The remaining seven cannon positions were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The other seven positions followed the same order.

sentences.zh: 副都統以次陪祀。

translations.literal: Lieutenant commanders assisted in order.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant commanders attended in succession.

sentences.zh: 聖祖凱旋，設壇德勝門外，祭品如祭纛。

translations.literal: On the Sacred Ancestor's triumphant return, an altar was set outside Desheng Gate; offerings as for standard sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On Kangxi's victorious return an altar was raised outside Desheng Gate, with offerings matching the standard rite.

sentences.zh: 世宗亦定三年一祭。

translations.literal: Shizong likewise fixed one sacrifice every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng fixed the same three-year interval.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，滿洲火器營始祭八旗子母砲神，總統承祭，如漢軍祀砲儀。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, the Manchu Firearms Camp first sacrificed to the Eight Banners mother-and-child cannon spirit; the superintendent officiated, as in the Han Army cannon ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 14 the Manchu Firearms Camp began sacrificing to the mother-and-child cannon of the Eight Banners—the superintendent officiating, mirroring the Han ritual.

sentences.zh: 其後定滿洲祀砲依漢軍例，季秋赴盧溝橋演砲，即以其日祭焉。

translations.literal: Later it was fixed that Manchu cannon sacrifice follow the Han Army precedent: in late autumn going to Lugou Bridge for cannon drill, sacrificing on that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Later Manchu cannon worship was aligned with the Han precedent: late-autumn drill at the Lugou Bridge doubled as the sacrificial day.

sentences.zh: 三十年，祀砲始用祝版，並專設祭器。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, cannon sacrifice first used prayer tablets and dedicated sacrificial vessels were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 prayer tablets were introduced and dedicated vessels provided.

sentences.zh: 群祀先醫，初沿明舊，致祭太醫院景惠殿，歲仲春上甲，遣官行禮。

translations.literal: Collective sacrifice: Progenitor of Medicine—initially following Ming practice, sacrifice at the Jinghui Hall of the Imperial Medical Academy, each year's first jia day of mid-spring, an officer dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Among collective sacrifices, the Progenitor of Medicine—following Ming custom—was honored at the Imperial Medical Academy's Jinghui Hall on the first jia day of mid-spring by a dispatched officer.

sentences.zh: 祀三皇，中伏羲，左神農，右黃帝。

translations.literal: Three Sovereigns were worshipped: Fuxi at center, Shennong left, Yellow Emperor right.
translations.idiomatic: Three Sovereigns were enshrined: Fuxi at center, Shennong to the left, the Yellow Emperor to the right.

sentences.zh: 四配：句芒、風后、祝融、力牧。

translations.literal: Four attendants: Goumang, Fenghou, Zhurong, Limu.
translations.idiomatic: Four flank figures: Goumang, Fenghou, Zhurong, and Limu.

sentences.zh: 東廡僦貸季、岐伯、伯高、少師、雷公、伊尹、淳于意、華陀、皇甫謐、巢元方、韋慈藏、錢乙、劉完素、李果十四人，西則鬼臾區、俞跗、少俞、桐君、馬師皇、扁鵲、張機、王叔和、葛洪、孫思邈、王冰、硃肱、張元素、硃彥修十四人。

translations.literal: The east corridor: Jiedaiji, Qibo, Bogao, Shaoshi, Leigong, Yi Yin, Chunyu Yi, Hua Tuo, Huangfu Mi, Chao Yuanfang, Wei Cizang, Qian Yi, Liu Wansu, Li Gao—fourteen; the west: Guiyuqu, Yu Fu, Shaoyu, Tongjun, Ma Shihuang, Bian Que, Zhang Ji, Wang Shuhe, Ge Hong, Sun Simiao, Wang Bing, Zhu Gong, Zhang Yuansu, Zhu Yanxiu—fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: East corridor: Jiedaiji, Qibo, Bogao, Shaoshi, Leigong, Yi Yin, Chunyu Yi, Hua Tuo, Huangfu Mi, Chao Yuanfang, Wei Cizang, Qian Yi, Liu Wansu, and Li Gao—fourteen in all. West: Guiyuqu, Yu Fu, Shaoyu, Tongjun, Ma Shihuang, Bian Que, Zhang Ji, Wang Shuhe, Ge Hong, Sun Simiao, Wang Bing, Zhu Gong, Zhang Yuansu, and Zhu Yanxiu—fourteen.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書承祭。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites performed the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites officiated.

sentences.zh: 兩廡分獻，以太醫院官。

translations.literal: The two corridors distributed offerings, by Imperial Medical Academy officers.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of the Imperial Medical Academy distributed offerings in the two side halls.

sentences.zh: 禮用三跪九拜。

translations.literal: The rite used three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The rite called for three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 三獻。

translations.literal: Three offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，命太醫院官咸致齋陪祀。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, Imperial Medical Academy officers were all ordered to fast and assist in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng all academy officers were required to fast and attend.

sentences.zh: 都城隍廟有二，舊瀋陽城隍廟，自元訖明，祀典勿替。

translations.literal: Capital city-god temples were two: the old Shenyang city-god temple, from Yuan through Ming, its sacrifices never discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: There were two capital city-god temples; the old Shenyang shrine had maintained its rites unbroken from Yuan through Ming.

sentences.zh: 清初建都後，升為都城隍廟，有司以時致祭。

translations.literal: After early Qing established the capital, it was elevated to Capital City-God Temple; local officers sacrificed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Once the early Qing court moved in, it became the Capital City-God Temple, with timely offerings from local officers.

sentences.zh: 其在燕京者，建廟宣武門內。

translations.literal: That in Yanjing was built inside Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanjing a temple was built inside Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 順治八年仲秋，遣太常卿致祭，歲以為常。

translations.literal: In mid-autumn of the eighth year of Shunzhi, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice-president was dispatched; yearly thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-autumn of Shunzhi 8 the Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice-president was sent annually.

sentences.zh: 用太牢，禮獻如祀先醫。

translations.literal: Tai lao was used; offerings and rite as for Progenitor of Medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were tai lao, the rite matching that for the Progenitor of Medicine.

sentences.zh: 萬壽節遣祭，加果品。

translations.literal: On Longevity Festival an envoy sacrifice was sent, with fruit added.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday an envoy was sent, with additional fruit.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，改遣大臣，嗣覆命親王行禮。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng, changed to dispatching a minister; later again ordered a prince to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng a minister was sent instead; later a prince was again ordered to officiate.

sentences.zh: 禁城城隍廟建城西北隅。

translations.literal: The Forbidden City city-god temple was built at the northwest corner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: A Forbidden City city-god shrine stood at the city's northwest corner.

sentences.zh: 皇城城隍廟建西安門內，曰永佑宮，萬壽節或季秋，遣內府大臣承祭，用少牢。

translations.literal: The Imperial City city-god temple was built inside Xi'an Gate, called Yongyou Palace; on Longevity Festival or late autumn, an Inner Palace grand minister officiated, using xiao lao.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Xi'an Gate stood the Imperial City shrine, Yongyou Palace; on the birthday or in late autumn an Inner Palace minister sacrificed with xiao lao.

sentences.zh: 北極佑聖真君廟，建地安門外日中坊橋東，曰靈明顯佑宮。

translations.literal: Temple of the Northern Pole Protecting Sage True Lord, built east of Rizhongfang Bridge outside Di'an Gate, called Lingming Xianyou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Pole Protecting Sage stood east of Rizhongfang Bridge outside Di'an Gate—the Lingming Xianyou Palace.

sentences.zh: 順治中，定制萬壽節遣官祭，後改遣大臣。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi the rule was fixed: Longevity Festival envoy sacrifice; later changed to dispatching a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi an officer was sent on the birthday; later a minister.

sentences.zh: 設果盤五、餅餌盤十五、茶餞三、行禮三跪九拜。

translations.literal: Five fruit trays, fifteen cake trays, three tea confections set out; rite of three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Five fruit trays, fifteen pastry trays, and three tea sweets were laid out; the rite was three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 火神廟，建日中坊橋西。

translations.literal: Fire God Temple, built west of Rizhongfang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Fire God Temple stood west of Rizhongfang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，定歲六月二十三日遣太常卿祭，後改遣大臣。

translations.literal: In early Kangxi fixed: each year on the twenty-third of the sixth month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice-president was dispatched; later changed to a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi fixed sacrifice on the sixth month's twenty-third day by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice-president; later by a minister.

sentences.zh: 用少牢。

translations.literal: Xiao lao was used.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were xiao lao.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，改太牢。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng, changed to tai lao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng this became tai lao.

sentences.zh: 帛初用白，乾隆中改用赤。

translations.literal: Silks initially white; in Qianlong changed to red.
translations.idiomatic: Silks were white at first; in Qianlong they turned red.

sentences.zh: 餘如祀北極儀。

translations.literal: The remainder as for Northern Pole rite.
translations.idiomatic: All else followed the Northern Pole rite.

sentences.zh: 東嶽廟，在朝陽門外，歲祭以萬壽節。

translations.literal: Eastern Peak Temple, outside Chaoyang Gate; yearly sacrifice on Longevity Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Peak Temple outside Chaoyang Gate was sacrificed to each year on the emperor's birthday.

sentences.zh: 龍神之祭，黑龍潭廟建西北金山巔，聖祖、世宗親制碑記。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Dragon Spirit: Black Dragon Pool Temple built on the summit of Northwest Gold Mountain; the Sacred Ancestor and Shizong personally composed stele inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon worship centered on the Black Dragon Pool Temple atop Northwest Gold Mountain—Kangxi and Yongzheng each wrote its stele.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，錫號「昭靈沛澤」。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong, granted the title "Manifest Spirit, Abundant Blessing."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 it received the title "Manifest Spirit, Abundant Blessing."

sentences.zh: 玉泉山廟，九年錫號「惠濟慈佑」。

translations.literal: Jade Spring Mountain Temple: in the ninth year granted "Blessing Relief, Merciful Protection."
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Spring Mountain shrine received "Blessing Relief, Merciful Protection" in year 9.

sentences.zh: 昆明湖祠，舊曰廣潤靈雨祠，錫號「安佑普濟」，嘉慶中，加「沛澤廣生」。

translations.literal: Kunming Lake shrine, formerly called Broad Moisture Spirit Rain Shrine, granted "Peaceful Blessing, Universal Relief"; in Jiaqing added "Abundant Blessing, Broad Generation."
translations.idiomatic: The Kunming Lake shrine—once the Broad Moisture Spirit Rain Temple—was titled "Peaceful Blessing, Universal Relief," and in Jiaqing gained "Abundant Blessing, Broad Generation."

sentences.zh: 京畿旱，帝親禱黑龍潭廟。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered drought, the emperor personally prayed at Black Dragon Pool Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During drought in the capital region the emperor prayed in person at the Black Dragon Pool.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年，錫號「昭靈廣濟」。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, granted "Manifest Spirit, Broad Relief."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46 it was titled "Manifest Spirit, Broad Relief."

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，始列祀典，遣散秩大臣往祭惠濟祠。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period, first entered the sacrificial canon; a minister without portfolio was dispatched to sacrifice at the Huiji Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing it entered the state canon; a minister without portfolio was sent to the Huiji Shrine.

sentences.zh: 河神廟建綺春園內，祀天后、龍神、河神，並春、秋致祭，遣圓明園大臣將事。

translations.literal: River God Temple built within Qichun Garden, worshipping Tianhou, Dragon Spirit, and River God; spring and autumn sacrifices, a Yuanmingyuan minister presiding.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Qichun Garden a River God Temple honored Tianhou, the Dragon Spirit, and the River God—spring and autumn—with a Yuanmingyuan minister presiding.

sentences.zh: 儀品俱視都城隍廟。

translations.literal: Rite and offerings all according to the Capital City-God Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Rite and offerings matched the Capital City-God Temple.

sentences.zh: 其祀之無定時、定所，及有司以時專祭者，后土司工之神，順治初制，凡大興作，因其方築左右壇，建采棚，遣官往祭，用少牢餅果。

translations.literal: Those sacrifices without fixed time or place, and those where local officers sacrifice on schedule alone: Queen Earth and the Minister of Works spirits—in early Shunzhi, for all major construction, according to the direction altars were built left and right of the work, colored sheds erected, an officer dispatched with xiao lao and cakes.
translations.idiomatic: For rites without fixed season or shrine, and for local officers' scheduled offerings alone: Queen Earth and the Minister of Works—in early Shunzhi, major construction called for altars on either side of the site, colored booths, and an officer with xiao lao and pastry.

sentences.zh: 若大工迎吻，祭琉璃窯神暨各門神，如祭司工禮。

translations.literal: For major works when receiving the ridge ornament, sacrifice to the glazed-kiln spirit and each gate spirit, as for Minister of Works rite.
translations.idiomatic: When major works reached the ridge-ornament ceremony, the glazed-kiln and gate spirits were honored as for the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，錫號圓明園春雨軒司工神曰昭休敷禧真君，土母曰夫人。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period, granted title to Yuanmingyuan Chunyu Pavilion Minister of Works spirit as "Manifest Rest, Spreading Joy True Lord"; Earth Mother as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianfeng the Yuanmingyuan Chunyu Pavilion Works Spirit was titled Manifest Rest, Spreading Joy True Lord; the Earth Mother, Lady.

sentences.zh: 命內府大臣春、秋奉祀。

translations.literal: Inner Palace grand ministers ordered to worship spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace ministers were charged with spring and autumn worship.

sentences.zh: 司機神，順治季年設織造局，始行祭告，禮部長官主之。

translations.literal: Spirit of the Loom: in the late Shunzhi years the Weaving Bureau was established; sacrifice-reporting first performed; the chief of the Board of Rites presided.
translations.idiomatic: The Loom Spirit—when the Weaving Bureau was founded late in Shunzhi—received inaugural sacrifice under the Board of Rites chief.

sentences.zh: 司倉神，通州三倉，舊惟西倉有祠。

translations.literal: Spirit of the Granary: Tongzhou's three granaries—formerly only the West Granary had a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Spirit: of Tongzhou's three granaries, only the West Granary once had a shrine.

sentences.zh: 京內七倉，惟右翼興平倉有祠，雍正間重葺。

translations.literal: Within the capital, seven granaries—only the Right Wing Xingping Granary had a shrine; rebuilt in the Yongzheng period.
translations.idiomatic: Of the seven granaries within the capital, only the Right Wing Xingping Granary possessed a shrine; it was rebuilt under Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 繇是左翼置廟海運倉。

translations.literal: Henceforth the Left Wing established a temple at the Sea Transport Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Left Wing erected a temple at the Sea Transport Granary.

sentences.zh: 京外五倉，置廟儲濟倉，並立神位。

translations.literal: The five granaries outside the capital—a temple was placed at the Store-and-Relief Granary, and spirit tablets were established together.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five granaries outside the capital, a temple was set up at the Store-and-Relief Granary, with spirit tablets installed.

sentences.zh: 倉場侍郎承祭，用少牢、果品，倉監督陪祀，二跪六拜。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of Granaries vice-minister presided; xiao lao and fruit were used; the granary supervisor assisted in worship—two kneelings and six prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice-Minister of Granaries presided, offering xiao lao and fruit; the granary superintendent assisted—two kneelings and six prostrations.

sentences.zh: 諸祭將事以黎明，與祭者咸朝服，此其大凡也。

translations.literal: All sacrifices were conducted at dawn; participants all wore court dress—such was the general practice.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices began at dawn; all participants wore court dress—such, in broad outline, was the practice.

sentences.zh: 至特旨建祠京師者，具見後簡。

translations.literal: As for those shrines specially ordered built in the capital, all are set forth in the appended summary.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines erected in the capital by special imperial order are catalogued in the appendix below.

sentences.zh: 若夫直省御災捍患有功德於民者，則錫封號，建專祠，所在有司秩祀如典。

translations.literal: As for those in the provinces who warded off calamity and guarded against harm and had merit for the people, titles were granted, dedicated shrines established, and local officers worshipped on schedule according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial figures who had shielded the people from disaster and rendered meritorious service received posthumous titles and dedicated shrines; local officials maintained scheduled worship as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 世祖朝，宿遷祀河神宋謝緒。

translations.literal: In the Shizu reign, Suqian worshipped the River God Song Xie Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, Suqian honored the River God Song Xie Xu of the Song.

sentences.zh: 聖祖朝，成都祀諸葛亮；

translations.literal: In the Shengzu reign, Chengdu worshipped Zhuge Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, Chengdu honored Zhuge Liang;

sentences.zh: 福建暨各省祀天后宋林氏女。

translations.literal: Fujian and each province worshipped Tianhou, the Song surname Lin maiden.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian and the other provinces honored Tianhou, the Lady Lin of Song.

sentences.zh: 世宗朝，各省祀猛將軍元劉承忠。

translations.literal: In the Shizong reign, each province worshipped Fierce General Liu Chengzhong of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, the provinces honored the Fierce General Liu Chengzhong of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 先是直隸總督李維鈞奏：「蝗災，土人禱猛將軍廟，患輒除。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhili Governor-General Li Weijun memorialized: "Locust plague—local people prayed at the Fierce General Temple, and the plague was promptly removed."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhili Governor-General Li Weijun reported: "During a locust plague, local people prayed at the Fierce General Temple and the infestation vanished.

sentences.zh: 於是下各省立廟祀。

translations.literal: Thereupon an order was sent to each province to establish temples and worship.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order then went out directing every province to build temples and offer worship.

sentences.zh: 已，兩江總督查弼納亦言：「猛將軍廟祀所在無蝗害，無廟處皆為災。」

translations.literal: Later, Liangjiang Governor-General Zha Bingna also said: "Where the Fierce General Temple is worshipped there is no locust harm; where there is no temple all suffer disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Later Liangjiang Governor-General Zha Bingna argued: "Places that maintained the Fierce General Temple escaped locust damage; those without shrines suffered.

sentences.zh: 被訶責。

translations.literal: He was rebuked and reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 詔言：「水旱蝗災，疆吏當修省，勿專事祈禱。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "For flood, drought, and locust calamities, frontier officials should cultivate self-examination—do not rely exclusively on prayer."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "In flood, drought, and locust crises, border officials must examine their own conduct—not lean solely on prayer.

sentences.zh: 錢塘祀伍員，封英衛公；

translations.literal: Qiantang worshipped Wu Yuan, granted title Heroic Guardian Duke;
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang honored Wu Yuan, titled Heroic Guardian Duke;

sentences.zh: 臨安祀錢鏐，封誠應王；

translations.literal: Lin'an worshipped Qian Liu, granted title Sincere Response King;
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an honored Qian Liu, titled Sincere Response King;

sentences.zh: 蕭山祀宋張夏，封靜安公；

translations.literal: Xiaoshan worshipped Song Zhang Xia, granted title Tranquil Peace Duke;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshan honored the Song official Zhang Xia, titled Tranquil Peace Duke;

sentences.zh: 紹興祀明知府湯紹忠，封寧江伯，後司事莫龍附焉；

translations.literal: Shaoxing worshipped Ming prefect Tang Shaozhong, granted title Tranquil River Earl; later the steward Mo Long was adjoined;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing honored the Ming prefect Tang Shaozhong, titled Tranquil River Earl; the steward Mo Long was later added;
