translations.literal: Guangxi worshipped Han Ma Yuan and Ming Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi honored Ma Yuan of Han and Wang Shouren of Ming.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十七年，兩宮西狩，迴鑾，御舟濟河，波濤不驚，特加大王、將軍諸封號。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Guangxu, the two palaces went west on hunt, returned the imperial carriage, the imperial boat crossed the river, the waves unstirred, specially enlarged the various titles of Great Kings and Generals.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 27, after the two empress dowagers' flight west and their return to the capital, the imperial boat crossed the river unperturbed by the waves; titles of Great Kings and Generals were specially extended.

sentences.zh: 凡予祀皆有封號，不悉紀，紀其著者。

translations.literal: Generally those granted worship all had posthumous titles; not all are recorded in full—only the notable ones are set down.
translations.idiomatic: All figures admitted to official worship received posthumous titles; not every case is recorded here—only the notable ones.

sentences.zh: 或前朝已封，今復加號，或當代始封，後屢加號，則悉略之。

translations.literal: Some had already been titled in earlier dynasties and now received additional titles; some were first titled in the present dynasty and later repeatedly augmented—these are all omitted in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Cases where an earlier dynasty had already bestowed titles later augmented, or where titles granted in the present reign were repeatedly extended, are all passed over.

sentences.zh: 定例，封號至四十字不復加，間有之，非常制，止金龍四大王四十字外加號錫祜，天后加至六十字，復錫以嘉佑云。

translations.literal: By established rule, when a title reached forty characters no further additions were made; occasionally there were exceptions, not the regular system—only the Four Great Kings of the Golden Dragon received additional title Bestow Blessings beyond forty characters, and Tianhou was extended to sixty characters, further granted Jia-you, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: By rule, titles stopped at forty characters; exceptions were rare. Only the Four Great Kings of the Golden Dragon received Bestow Blessings beyond forty characters, and Tianhou's title reached sixty, further augmented with Jia-you.

sentences.zh: 五祀，初循舊制，每歲暮合祭太廟西廡下。

translations.literal: The Five Sacrifices: initially following the old system, at year's end they were jointly offered beneath the west corridor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Sacrifices: at first the old practice was kept—a joint offering each year-end beneath the west side hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 順治八年定制，歲孟春宮門外祭司戶神，孟夏大庖前祭司灶神，季夏太和殿階祭中霤神，孟秋午門西祭司門神，孟冬大庖井前祭司井神，中霤門、午門二祀，太常寺掌之，戶、灶、井三祀，內務府掌之，於是始分祭，旋復故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: in the first month of spring the Door Spirit was sacrificed to outside the palace gate; in the first month of summer the Kitchen Spirit before the great kitchen; in the last month of summer the Central Eaves Spirit on the steps of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; in the first month of autumn the Gate Spirit west of the Meridian Gate; in the first month of winter the Well Spirit before the great kitchen well—the Central Eaves and Gate sacrifices were managed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Door, Kitchen, and Well three sacrifices by the Imperial Household Department; thus separate sacrifices began, but soon the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 fixed regulations divided the rites: in early spring the Door Spirit outside the palace gate; in early summer the Kitchen Spirit before the great kitchen; in late summer the Central Eaves Spirit on the steps of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; in early autumn the Gate Spirit west of the Meridian Gate; in early winter the Well Spirit before the great kitchen well. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices managed the Central Eaves and Gate offerings; the Imperial Household Department managed the Door, Kitchen, and Well. Separate observances began—and were soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 逮聖祖釐祀典，再罷之，並停專祀。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor reformed the sacrificial canon, he abolished them again and also halted their dedicated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangxi reformed the ritual canon, he abolished them again and ended their separate observances altogether.

sentences.zh: 惟十二月二十三日，宮中祀灶以為常。

translations.literal: Only on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month was the Kitchen Spirit worshipped in the palace as customary.
translations.idiomatic: Only the palace sacrifice to the Kitchen Spirit on the twenty-third of the twelfth month remained as custom.

sentences.zh: 八蜡之祭，清初關外舉行，廟建南門內，春、秋設壇望祭。

translations.literal: The Eight La sacrifice: in early Qing it was conducted outside the pass; a temple was built inside the South Gate, and in spring and autumn an altar was set up for distant offering.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight La rite was observed in the Qing beyond the pass; a shrine inside the South Gate served spring and autumn distant offerings at an outdoor altar.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，猶踵行之。

translations.literal: When Shizu entered the pass, he still followed it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shunzhi entered China proper, the practice continued.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，詔罷蜡祭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong, an edict abolished the La sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 an edict abolished the La rite.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣猶力請行古蜡祭，高宗諭曰：「大蜡之禮，昉自伊耆，三代因之，古制夐遠，傳注參錯。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers still strenuously petitioned to conduct the ancient La sacrifice; the High Ancestor instructed: "The great La rite originated with Yixu; the Three Dynasties followed it—the ancient system is remote, and the commentaries conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Still petitioning for the ancient La rite, court ministers received Qianlong's reply: "The great La ceremony began with Yixu and was continued through the Three Dynasties; the old forms lie far off, and the transmitted glosses contradict one another.

sentences.zh: 八蜡配以昆蟲，後儒謂害稼不當祭。

translations.literal: The Eight La paired with insects; later Ruists held that those harming crops should not be sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight La included insects among the offerings—later scholars argued that pests deserving the harvest ought not be worshipped.

sentences.zh: 月令：『祈年於天宗。』

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: 'Pray for the year's harvest at the Heavenly Ancestor.'
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances: 'Pray for the year's harvest at the Heavenly Ancestor.'

sentences.zh: 蜡祭也。

translations.literal: —this is the La sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: —this is the La sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 注云『日、月、星、辰』，則所主又非八神。

translations.literal: The annotation says 'sun, moon, stars, and constellations'—then the principal deities are again not the Eight Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The annotation reads 'sun, moon, stars, and constellations'—so the principal deities are not the Eight Spirits at all.

sentences.zh: 至謂合聚萬物而索饗之，神多位益難定。

translations.literal: Moreover, to say that all things are gathered and a feast demanded of them—the spirits are many and their ranks increasingly hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: To say that all things are gathered and a feast demanded of them is worse still—the spirits are many, and their ranks impossible to fix.

sentences.zh: 蠟與臘冠服各殊，或謂臘即蠟，或謂蠟而後臘。

translations.literal: La (wax) and La (twelfth month) differ in caps and robes; some say the twelfth month is the wax rite, others that wax comes before the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: The wax rite and the twelfth-month rite differ in caps and robes; some hold the twelfth month is the wax rite, others that wax precedes the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 自漢臘而不蠟，魏、晉以降，廢置無恆。

translations.literal: From Han onward there was the twelfth-month rite but not the wax rite; from Wei and Jin downward, abolition and restoration were unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: From Han onward the twelfth-month rite survived without the wax rite; from Wei and Jin downward, abolition and restoration followed no steady course.

sentences.zh: 或溺五行家言，甚至天帝、人帝及龍、麟、硃鳥，為座百九十二，議者謂失禮。

translations.literal: Some drowned in Five Phases school talk, going so far as Heavenly Emperor, Human Emperor, dragon, qilin, and vermilion bird—one hundred ninety-two seats; critics called it a breach of rite.
translations.idiomatic: Some drowned in Five Phases doctrine, seating as many as one hundred ninety-two figures—Heavenly Emperor, Human Emperor, dragon, qilin, and vermilion bird—critics called it a breach of rite.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾曰：『迎貓則為貓屍，迎虎則為虎屍，近俳優所為。』

translations.literal: Su Shi said: 'If you welcome the cat you get a cat corpse; if you welcome the tiger you get a tiger corpse—it resembles what players do.'
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said: 'If you welcome the cat you get a cat corpse; if you welcome the tiger you get a tiger corpse—it resembles what players do.'

sentences.zh: 是其跡久類於戲也，是以元、明廢止不行。

translations.literal: Such conduct had long resembled play, hence Yuan and Ming abolished it and did not perform it.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct had long resembled play, hence Yuan and Ming abolished it and did not perform it.

sentences.zh: 況蜡祭諸神，如先嗇、司嗇、日、月、星、辰、山、林、川、澤，祀之各壇廟，民間報賽，亦借蜡祭聯歡井閭。

translations.literal: Moreover the spirits of the La sacrifice—such as First Reaper, Reaper Official, sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes—each has its own altar or temple; popular thanksgiving also borrowed the La sacrifice for communal festivity in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the spirits of the La rite—First Reaper, Reaper Official, sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes—each has its own altar or temple; popular thanksgiving also borrowed the La rite for communal festivity in the lanes.

sentences.zh: 但各隨其風尚，初不責以儀文，其悉罷之。」

translations.literal: But each follows local custom and was never bound to formal ritual—abolish them all."
translations.idiomatic: But each follows local custom and was never bound to formal ritual—abolish them all."

sentences.zh: 自是無復蜡祭矣。

translations.literal: From then on there was no La sacrifice again.
translations.idiomatic: From then on there was no La sacrifice again.

sentences.zh: 祭厲明制，自京師訖郡、縣，皆祭厲壇。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to wandering spirits was a Ming institution; from the capital down to prefectures and counties, all had Wandering Spirit altars.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to wandering spirits was a Ming institution; from the capital down to prefectures and counties, all maintained Wandering Spirit altars.

sentences.zh: 清初建都盛京，厲壇建地載門外。

translations.literal: In early Qing the capital was established at Shengjing; the Wandering Spirit altar was built outside the Dizai Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qing the capital was established at Shengjing; the Wandering Spirit altar stood outside the Dizai Gate.

sentences.zh: 自世祖入關後，京師祭厲無聞焉。

translations.literal: From the time Shizu entered the pass, nothing more was heard of the capital's Wandering Spirit sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After Shunzhi entered China proper, the capital's Wandering Spirit sacrifice was heard of no more.

sentences.zh: 唯直省城隍合祀神祇壇，月朔、望有司詣廟上香，二跪六拜，暘雨愆期則禱。

translations.literal: Only in the direct provinces, at the City God joint-worship Spirit Altar, on the first and fifteenth of the month officials went to the temple to offer incense, two kneelings and six prostrations; when drought or rain was untimely they prayed.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the direct provinces, at the City God joint-worship Spirit Altar, officials offered incense on the first and fifteenth of each month with two kneelings and six prostrations; when drought or rain fell out of season they prayed.

sentences.zh: 復以城隍主厲壇祀。

translations.literal: The City God was again made master of the Wandering Spirit altar worship.
translations.idiomatic: The City God was again made master of the Wandering Spirit altar.

sentences.zh: 順治初，直省府、州、縣設壇城北郊，歲以清明日、七月十五日、十月朔日，用羊三、豕三、米飯三石、香燭、酒醴、楮帛祭本境無祀鬼神。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, in direct-province prefectures, departments, and counties an altar was set up in the northern suburb; each year on Qingming, the fifteenth of the seventh month, and the first of the tenth month, with three sheep, three pigs, three shi of rice, incense, candles, wine, and silks they sacrificed to un-worshipped spirits within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, direct-province prefectures, departments, and counties set up altars in the northern suburbs; each year on Qingming, the fifteenth of the seventh month, and the first of the tenth month they sacrificed with three sheep, three pigs, three shi of rice, incense, candles, wine, and silks to spirits within the jurisdiction who lacked worship.

sentences.zh: 府曰郡厲，縣曰邑厲。

translations.literal: In a prefecture it was called Commandery Wandering; in a county, District Wandering.
translations.idiomatic: In a prefecture it was called Commandery Wandering; in a county, District Wandering.

sentences.zh: 先期備祭物，有司詣城隍廟以祭厲告。

translations.literal: In advance sacrificial items were prepared; officials went to the City God temple to announce the Wandering Spirit sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial items were prepared in advance; officials went to the City God temple to announce the Wandering Spirit rite.

sentences.zh: 屆日設燎爐壇南，奉城隍神位安壇正中。

translations.literal: On the appointed day a brazier was set south of the altar and the City God spirit tablet was placed at the altar's center.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day a brazier was set south of the altar and the City God spirit tablet placed at its center.

sentences.zh: 詣神位前跪，三上香，行禮用三拜。

translations.literal: Approaching before the spirit tablet they knelt, thrice offered incense, and performed the rite with three prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Before the spirit tablet they knelt, offered incense three times, and performed three prostrations.

sentences.zh: 送燎，奠三爵，退，神位復初。

translations.literal: The brazier was sent off, three libations were poured, they withdrew, and the spirit tablet was restored to its place.
translations.idiomatic: The brazier was sent off, three libations poured, they withdrew, and the spirit tablet was restored to its place.
